name: Fix optical magnification source resolution
description:
## Goal
Fix Critic R2: refractive-lens and focal Magnify soften text because they enlarge native-resolution source textures with linear filtering.

## Evidence
- Critic recommendation: IMPLEMENTATION-FIX-REQUIRED
- Refractive lens: p0.25 at (1510,260), normalized edge step 0.8396 vs native 0.9866
- Focal Magnify: p0.15 at (2150,620), normalized edge step 0.8389 vs native 0.9978
- Responsible paths: src/lib/pipelines/effects/refractive-lens/index.ts and src/lib/pipelines/surfaces/paper/pipeline.ts

## Requirements
- Fix source resolution in the rendering pipeline; do not reduce authored magnification in Preset JSON.
- Preserve native 3840x2160 / 2160x3840 output, premultiplied alpha, frame determinism, preview/export parity, and outside-region pixel identity.
- Apply one coherent resolution strategy to the composition Effect and focal Annotation paths.

## Done when
- Focused tests and static gates pass.
- Native flagged-Chrome captures have no WGSL/runtime errors.
- R2 probe no longer reports softened transformed text.
- Fresh isolated Critic returns ACCEPT with zero pipeline-bug/default-too-permissive findings.
result: Replaced linear optical enlargement with shared sharp cubic reconstruction in refractive-lens and Magnify. Final Critic measured transformed text equal to native sharpness in both orientations; focused tests, check, preset verification, build, and native captures pass.

name: Tighten the docs-site design
description:
## Context
Scott, on approving the hero video (2026-09-01): "i just need the design to be tightened up." The site's content architecture is now right (product pages, hero video, pack showcase incoming); this pass makes the design feel deliberate everywhere. GFX brand identity: the Slate, warm blacks + one loud yellow, Space Grotesk/Space Mono voices, matte, no gloss (see docs/identity and the Syntax pack language the site already borrows).

## Work
A whole-site polish pass on docs-site — spacing, hierarchy, and consistency, not new features:
- One spacing scale applied consistently (hero, bands, doc pages, packs sections) — kill ad-hoc margins.
- Typographic rhythm: heading sizes/weights consistent across home, doc pages, /packs; measure (line length) capped consistently; the mono-label voice used deliberately, not decoratively.
- Hero: balance the workspace-video block against the headline; ensure the video's poster/first frame composes with the frame corners; check mobile.
- Bands (preset loops, doors, layers): consistent gutters, aligned baselines, identical card treatment; hover states consistent (border-only, no glows — matte).
- Doc pages: TOC/kicker/prose column alignment, code-block and table styling consistent with the home aesthetic.
- Dark theme only is fine (site already commits to it) — make backgrounds/borders one token set, not scattered hexes.
- Mobile: every page reads clean at 390px; no horizontal scroll.

## Constraints
- No new pages, no content changes, no framework/tooling changes.
- Matte discipline: no gradients (unless already in the identity), no glows, no glassy anything.
- Keep CSS systemic — tokens/vars over one-off values.

## Verification
- docs-site suite green; before/after captures of /, a doc page, and /packs at 1440 and 390 recorded for the aesthetic gate.

name: Lock the WebMCP operation, transaction, and security contract
description:
## Scope
Define non-overlapping domain tool families for full create/open/inspect/edit/design/seek/validate/verify/export; dynamic registration; schema/registry derivation; expected revisions; atomic receipts; UI focus; undo/redo; cancellation; annotations; character budgets; origin exposure; file consent; and corrective errors. Forbid UI verbs and raw unbounded patching.

## Done when
The contract covers every accepted capability with clear ownership and preconditions, supplies a machine-readable operation inventory for parity tests, and resolves every WebMCP security and lifecycle decision needed by implementation.
result: ADR-0054 locks the WebMCP operation/transaction/security contract with machine-readable inventory: 15 non-overlapping operation families (pointer-ownership based, longest-pointer-wins), revisioned atomic transactions (observed revision, preflight, all-or-nothing, bounded receipts, shared undo stack with GUI, mandatory focus move), state-aware registration with cold-page ceiling, registry-derived schemas, character budgets, same-origin-only security, untrusted content annotation, corrective error codes. UI verbs and raw patching forbidden and enforced on tool names. webmcp-operation-inventory.ts: 78 rows mapping every operation to family/tool/pointers/preconditions/GUI surface — the parity gate's input.

commit.message: Lock the WebMCP operation, transaction, and security contract

name: Google Fonts catalog manifest + font-claim validation
description:
## Context
ADR-0055 (docs/adr/0055-user-defined-packs.md) fonts decision: user packs may claim any Google Fonts family, but claims validate offline against a vendored catalog snapshot — never at runtime against the network — and the playbook law holds: never synthesize weight or stretch (docs/packs/authoring-playbook.md §2.2).

## Work
1. `scripts/refresh-google-fonts-catalog.mjs` — regenerate a vendored snapshot of the Google Fonts metadata (per family: real static weights, styles, variable axes with ranges, woff2 file URLs) into `src/lib/platform/google-fonts-catalog.json`. Deliberate manual refresh only; the snapshot is committed data, never fetched at build or runtime.
2. `src/lib/platform/google-fonts-catalog.ts` — typed loader + lookup helpers (explicit return types, no `any`): family existence; whether a claimed weight/style is a real static cut or inside a declared variable axis range; resolve the exact file URL set for a `PackFont` claim.
3. Extend `src/lib/platform/packs/validation.ts` with a catalog-aware font check applied to user pack documents: every `PackFont` claim must resolve to real cuts or fail with a named issue. Builtin registry packs are exempt (their fonts are @fontsource-bundled and boot-gated already).

## Constraints
Strict TS; keep the module in `src/lib/platform/` (domain logic, not a generic utility); no new utility folders; snapshot size kept sane (metadata only, no font bytes).

## Verification
Colocated `google-fonts-catalog.test.ts` over a fixture subset (real cut accepted, fake cut refused, variable-axis range accepted); validation tests for the new issue kind; `pnpm check` + `pnpm test` green.
result: Vendored Google Fonts catalog (scripts/refresh-google-fonts-catalog.mjs -> src/lib/platform/google-fonts-catalog.json, 1946 families), typed loader google-fonts-catalog.ts with static/variable cut resolution, validateUserPackFontClaims + validateUserPackManifest in packs/validation.ts; builtins exempt. Snapshot holds no file URLs by decision: URLs resolve at save time.

commit.message: feat(packs): vendored Google Fonts catalog and user-pack font-claim validation

name: Phase 2 · The Stage in the Workspace — stage rows, stage inspectors, the body as an entity, the camera by hand
description: Approved by Scott 2026-09-02 after the physical-screen slice landed: 'nothing is reflected in the UI, the timeline is just a surface' — and 'I want this to work well enough that we can do some crazy stuff with it eventually.' Decided in ADR-0060 (docs/adr/0060-the-stage-in-the-workspace.md). Ordered before dimensional type (8q4v3l8d), because every later body needs the entity machinery this builds. Scope: (1) Camera and Focus rows at the top of the timeline outline plus one row per body, with the travel and the rack focus as window clips, vertical-camera aware; (2) every timeline drag records one undo entry; (3) Camera, Focus, and Screen inspectors reached by selection, the root keeping only the stage switch and backdrop, with appearance.set-stage-camera and appearance.set-stage-focus as operations and stage focus targets; (4) the body as a canvas entity — a projected selection region from the mesh bounds ranked below the page, an outline, its inspector; (5) orbit by dragging the body, dolly by wheel at fit zoom, page-grab reframing kept, clamped to STAGE_CAMERA_POSE_LIMITS, undoable; (6) closeout with the gfx-review human gate. Not a scene tree, no keyframed camera channels (ADR-0057 holds), no 3D workspace, no helper copy. Verification: pnpm check, pnpm test, pnpm verify-presets, pnpm audit:webmcp-parity, pnpm audit:parity, pnpm audit:planning; visual changes go through gfx-review.
result: Phase 2 · The Stage in the Workspace: all six leaves landed on main at 4a4bc93 — stage rows, timeline undo, stage inspectors and the camera/focus Operations, the body as a canvas entity, orbit by hand, closeout. Dimensional type (8q4v3l8d) is unblocked.

name: Chrome 153 WebMCP lifecycle and bounded tool disclosure
description:
## Goal
Align GFX with the current Chrome 153 WebMCP imperative API while reducing the open-composition context surface without weakening one-operation/one-tool authoring.

## Decisions
- Chrome 153 is the only supported WebMCP lifecycle contract.
- Keep the deterministic lexical and browser transport evals; a model-in-the-loop eval is intentionally out of scope.
- Keep existing storage-native arguments for compatibility, while accepting nested content objects and direct human time units.
- Keep a small core tool set registered and expose one authoring family at a time through an agent-context operation.
- Add standard readOnlyHint and untrustedContentHint annotations.
- Rewrite negative tool descriptions in positive language where consequences remain clear.

## Contract
Amend ADR-0054 and the operation inventory. Agent-context disclosure changes only WebMCP context, never composition or GUI state, and is therefore outside GUI/agent authoring parity. All authoring operations remain shared with the GUI.

## Verification
Run pnpm audit:planning, pnpm audit:webmcp-parity, focused WebMCP tests, pnpm check, pnpm test, and the sanctioned Chrome 153 browser eval when a Chrome 153 harness is available.
result: Shipped Chrome 153 WebMCP lifecycle compatibility, bounded core plus one prepared family, standard annotation hints, positive tool summaries, and compatible human-shaped time/content inputs. Deterministic checks and the real Chrome 153 production-build eval pass.

commit.message: feat: align WebMCP with Chrome 153

name: Accept human-shaped WebMCP arguments
description: Keep existing storage-native arguments, accept nested objects instead of JSON text for dynamic content, and accept direct seconds/timecode alternatives where timing currently requires frame or fraction arithmetic. Normalize inside operation code and add corrective tests.
result: Kept legacy fractions, frames, and JSON text while adding direct seconds/milliseconds/frames/timecode and nested runtime objects. Operations normalize to deterministic stored values; motion, content choreography, stage focus, sound, media, and playhead tests cover the new forms.

commit.message: feat: align WebMCP with Chrome 153

name: Make canvas element selection forgiving and predictable
description:
Implement bounded screen-space hit regions for thin, small, and transparent selectable elements using the shared interaction geometry contract. Preserve visual bounds while padding only pointer targets. Add deterministic overlap resolution and a clear way to cycle or otherwise choose the intended element when bounds overlap, following the existing selection model. Add restrained hover and selected outlines that never appear in exports. Acceptance: selection is reliable at every supported canvas zoom and in both orientations; ordering is stable; pointer tests cover transparent content, thin geometry, overlap, and drag initiation.

## Implementation evidence (2026-08-26)
- Added clipped 4px/24px-minimum screen-space pointer regions while keeping outlines on observed visual bounds.
- Added shared topmost ordering, Alt/Option overlap cycling, and current-choice retention so a cycled lower element starts a normal drag.
- Added transform/reflow remeasurement across 50%, 75%, 100%, 150%, 200%, 300%, and 400% zoom plus horizontal/vertical orientation.
- Added deterministic tests for transparent, thin, overlap, cycling, and padded drag initiation.
- Verification passed: 890 Vitest tests, svelte-check, touched-file ESLint, discoverability, production build, and flag-enabled CDP pointer/zoom/orientation/overlap checks with no console errors.
- Human approved the exact visual evidence at .tmp-baselines/canvas-selection/verification.png. Machine receipts: all-zooms.json and overlap.json in the same directory.
result:
Implemented forgiving, predictable canvas selection.

Changed:
- Added clipped 4px padding and 24px minimum screen-space pointer regions while preserving observed visual bounds.
- Added deterministic topmost overlap ordering, Alt/Option cycling, and current-choice retention so cycled lower elements start normal drags.
- Re-measures editor geometry through zoom transitions, panning, orientation changes, and workspace reflow.
- Kept restrained hover/focus/selected outlines in the editor-only CanvasEditingOverlay.
- Added tests for transparent content, thin geometry, padded drag initiation, stable overlap ordering, cycling, and subsequent selection retention.

Verified:
- Vitest: 123 files, 890 tests passed.
- svelte-check: 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- Touched-file ESLint and git diff check passed.
- Discoverability check passed.
- Production build passed.
- Flag-enabled CDP verified padding selection, drag initiation, every supported zoom (50/75/100/150/200/300/400%), horizontal and vertical reflow, clipped canvas bounds, deterministic overlap cycling, subsequent normal drag, and a clean console.
- Human approved the exact visual evidence at .tmp-baselines/canvas-selection/verification.png on 2026-08-26. Machine receipts: all-zooms.json and overlap.json in the same directory.

Repository-wide npm run check remains blocked only by two pre-existing ESLint errors in scripts/change-impact-classifier.ts and scripts/supers-delivery-routing-workflows.test.mjs; modified files lint cleanly.

name: Repair GFX-COMPUTER-12 from Sentry evidence
description:
Sentry GFX-COMPUTER-12: TypeError: Failed to fetch (localhost:7263), 10 events across 2026-08-03 -> 2026-08-27 and multiple releases (19d1ec19 -> 3b69fc83), transaction /p/[slug], handled=no, mechanism auto.function.sveltekit.handle_error. Evidence event 2026-08-27T00:53:54Z, release supers@3b69fc83d82d88142e65d2d78dd3925c88627708.

Frames are all SvelteKit client runtime: Module.start -> navigate -> load_route -> load_data -> dev_fetch -> window.fetch. Breadcrumbs pin the failing request to GET /p/docu-stat-build/__data.json?x-sveltekit-invalidated=01 followed by 'The next HMR update will cause the page to reload' — the origin went away under the tab while hydration was fetching its load data.

Root cause class: the origin restarting or rebuilding under an open tab. CLAUDE.md rebuilds and restarts gfx.robo.online after every integration, so this recurs by design. ADR-0058 already defines the recovery for the module half of this (vite:preloadError -> staleBuildRecovery.reloadIfBuildIsStale), but the client handleError in hooks.client.ts is a bare Sentry.handleErrorWithSentry() with no boundary: a load-data transport failure gets no recovery and is filed as an unhandled application error. Contrast hooks.server.ts, which has a considered capture boundary.

Fix: extend the ADR-0058 recovery to the navigation transport half — match an origin-unreachable fetch failure in src/lib/utils/stale-build-recovery.ts next to isModuleLoadFailure, and in hooks.client.ts funnel it into staleBuildRecovery.reloadIfBuildIsStale(), suppressing the Sentry event only when the tab is actually reloading onto a newer build. A genuine origin outage still reports.
result: hooks.client.ts now owns handleError instead of handing it straight to Sentry. A load whose own __data.json fetch never reached the origin (isOriginFetchFailure, new in src/lib/utils/stale-build-recovery.ts beside isModuleLoadFailure) takes the ADR-0058 staleBuildRecovery.reloadIfBuildIsStale() path and is reported only when the tab is not reloading; a genuinely unreachable origin still reports, since the version check has to reach that same origin. On a development host it is answered without either, because SvelteKit hard-wires updated.check() to false under __SVELTEKIT_DEV__ so a dev tab can never learn the dev server restarted, Vite's client already reloads on reconnect, and a dev server that went away is the only thing producing that message there — which is where all 10 events came from. isOriginFetchFailure matches the whole message so a dynamic import's 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: <url>' stays with isModuleLoadFailure; three cases pinned in stale-build-recovery.test.ts. ADR-0058 gains decision layer 4 and the unreachable-origin consequence. Gates: pnpm check green, pnpm test 223 files / 2169 tests green; no preset, pack, or pipeline file touched so verify-presets does not apply. Landed on dev (WebMCP Challenge rule), gfx-verify.rebuild_and_smoke green at 5b1a12a (build 12.2s, restart ok, / 200, /api/health 200). Sentry GFX-COMPUTER-12 resolved. Not pushed to origin/dev — left for Scott. Note: Seer's plan for this issue was wrong (it read fetcher.js's window.fetch frame as app code and proposed destructuring fetch in /p/[slug]'s load; those load functions contain no fetch at all).

commit.message: fix(sentry): recover a navigation whose load data never reached the origin

name: Effect animation schema, schema-derived channels, and cascade resolution
description:
## Scope
Context: ADR-0063 §1–§4, §6, §7 (`docs/adr/0063-keyframed-effect-parameters.md`). Today `EffectSchema` in `src/lib/platform/engine-schema.ts` (near line 1192) is `{ type, id, params: unknown }`, and each Effect's params are validated once by its `EffectPipelineDefinition.schema` (`src/lib/platform/pipelines/definition-types.ts`). ADR-0035 channels exist only on Overlays, the Surface, and Diagram primitives (`createKeyframeTrackSchema`, `OverlayChannelKeyframesSchema` in `engine-schema.ts`); cascade resolution lives in `src/lib/platform/cascade-timing.ts`.

Build:
- `EffectSchema` gains `animation?: z.strictObject({ channels?: <record of channel path → keyframe track>, cascade?: CascadeSchema })`. A track is the existing `createKeyframeTrackSchema` shape (strictly ascending `atMs`, first keyframe without `ease`, at least one keyframe). Channel names and value bounds are validated in `validatePresetSemantics` (`src/lib/platform/preset.ts`) against the effect's channel list: unknown channel, frozen channel, value outside the schema's min/max, or a non-integer value on an integer channel is a path-qualified parse error.
- A pure schema walker in `src/lib/utils/` (for example `zod-numeric-leaves.ts` with `listNumericLeafPaths(schema)`), unwrapping ZodOptional, ZodDefault, ZodNullable and ZodEffects (refine) and descending ZodObject, returning `{ path: 'melt.radius', min?, max?, isInteger }[]`. Check `src/lib/utils/` first for an existing zod or object-path helper to extend. Colocated test.
- `src/lib/platform/effect-keyframe-channels.ts`: `listEffectKeyframeChannels(definition)` returns the numeric leaves of the definition's params schema minus `definition.frozenParams`. `EffectPipelineDefinition` gains `frozenParams?: readonly string[]` with a doc comment above it: params that seed a fixed-step simulation, a replay, or a hash never become channels, because `SeekableSimulationRuntime` (`src/lib/platform/seekable-simulation-runtime.ts`) continues forward seeks from the current state and a kernel input that changed mid-run would make a jump-seek and a play-through disagree. Declare it on every definition with a `seed`, and on the kernel inputs of fluid-ripple (`damping`, `waveSpeed`; see `resolveFluidState` in its `index.ts`), cloth-bend (`stiffness`, `damping`; see `resolveClothState`), seeded-shatter and tiled-deformation. Read each `src/lib/pipelines/effects/*/definition.ts` and freeze exactly the kernel inputs, nothing more.
- `resolveCascadeTimings` adds an `effect:<id>` pending node for every authored effect that has channels or a cascade: base start 0, duration = `channelEnvelopeSpanMs(channels) / durationMs`, cascade from `effect.animation.cascade`. `cascadeNodeKey` and `CascadeAnchorSchema` stay unchanged: effects are subjects, never anchors. The parse-time cascade-cycle validator in `engine-schema.ts` must include effect edges.
- `src/lib/platform/composition-authoring-dependencies.ts` tracks effect channels the way it tracks overlay channels.
- Regenerate `docs/preset-format.schema.json` with `pnpm gen:schema`.
- Docs in the same change: `docs/preset-format.md` § `effects` (the `animation` block; a channel is a numeric leaf of the params schema by dotted path; frozen params; `atMs` from composition start; cascade as subject) and § `animation` (an Effect row in the channel table); `docs/CONTEXT.md` wherever it defines channel or keyframe so Effect params are included. Add one sentence to preset-format saying a declared effect channel validates but does not yet drive the render until the runtime leaf lands; the runtime leaf removes that sentence.

Constraints: strict TypeScript, no `any`; utilities only in `src/lib/utils/`; never restate a channel list per effect; no runtime behavior in this leaf.

## Done when
`pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify-presets` are green. `engine-schema.test.ts` covers accept and reject cases: unknown channel, frozen channel, out-of-bounds value, non-integer on an integer channel, a cascade cycle through an effect, and byte-identical round-trip of an effect with channels. `cascade-timing.test.ts` covers an effect welded to an overlay's enter end. The utils walker test covers optional, default, refine, and nested objects. `pnpm audit:planning` is green.

name: paper-grain invisible on near-black fields (additive option / lift dark bumpers)
description: From the text-3d Critic (2026-06-21, non-gating aesthetic-miss). paper-grain is MULTIPLICATIVE (out = rgb*(1±0.06*density)); on a near-black backgroundFill like #040408 (luma ~0.018) the per-frame shimmer is ~0.0002 luma = below visibility. So even after the effect-chain fix (grain now reaches the opaque backgroundFill), the grain reads as nothing on dark bumpers — verified background-only region 0 changed px on text-3d. The dark full-frame bumpers (text-3d, counter, instance-stack, cursor-trail, all on #040408) get NO living grain layer. Options: (a) add an ADDITIVE grain mode/term so grain is visible on near-black, or (b) lift the bumper fields slightly off pure-black (graded backdrop) so multiplicative grain + tone have something to live in. Pairs with the systemic 'flat CSS on black' audit deficit — these 4 bumpers have flat #040408 voids vs the graded backdrops the surfaces got. Low priority; the bumpers are Critic-ACCEPTed (foreground motion carries their holds).
result: Option (a) shipped: paper-grain gains a lift param (zod default 0 → byte-identical for every existing composition; x + 0·grain is bit-exact). lift couples the same two-octave grain field ADDITIVELY, weighted (alpha − luma) — full on opaque near-black, zero on bright content and transparent pixels (premultiplied-correct, E4 holds). Editor slider shipped with it (parity); pack() guards missing lift with ?? 0 for the raw-manifest pack-chrome lane. The three dark bumpers still authoring grain (counter-milestone, cursor-trail-title-sweep, instance-stack-vertical) author lift 0.3; text-3d no longer carries grain post-re-dress. Verified on counter-milestone 4K CDP captures: field liveness went 2% of px (dither-level, the dead field this task described) → 48% at max ±2/255; delta-by-luma monotone 0.37→0.09; amplified crops show organic structure that also masks field banding; frame at 1x still reads flat warm-black (Q12/brand-safe). NOTE: a stale local user-composition shadows cursor-trail-title-sweep in the GUI (loads instead of the corpus JSON) — known user-comp staleness class, not addressed here.

name: Add a realistic optical-vignette Effect
description:
## Goal
Add an ordinary post-process Effect named `optical-vignette` that reproduces believable lens edge falloff. It must read as real optics, not as a black radial-gradient overlay, and remain useful as a restrained finishing treatment.

## Scope and approach
- Implement the Effect under `src/lib/pipelines/effects/optical-vignette/` with a renderer-free typed definition, lazy TypeGPU/WGSL renderer, and a focused editor.
- Model a smooth, monotonic, aspect-correct screen-space falloff from an adjustable optical center. Use a cos^4-like exposure response or an equivalently defensible lens model, with bounded controls for exposure loss, onset/midpoint, feather, roundness, and center.
- Defaults must be subtle and production-usable. Zero strength must be a true no-op; the default must avoid hard rings, crushed corners, color shifts, visible banding, and an obviously synthetic ellipse in both native orientations.
- Multiply premultiplied RGB while preserving input alpha exactly. Never paint transparent pixels or introduce a background fill. As an ordinary Effect it must remain in the existing GFX-before-footage chain, so creator footage is not graded.
- Keep the result frame-deterministic and Pack-neutral. Do not add wall-clock animation, randomness, per-orientation variants, or Pack-specific appearance.
- Register the definition in `src/lib/platform/pipelines/definition-registry.ts` and the lazy renderer in `src/lib/platform/pipelines/runtime-loader.ts`. The existing registry-derived GUI and WebMCP Effect operations must discover `optical-vignette`; do not add a gesture-level or raw-patch operation.
- Add an `Editor.svelte` whose controls do not mutate absent/defaulted params on mount. Follow current Svelte 5 and Graffiti patterns.
- Add focused schema/registry/renderer tests and a Pack-neutral `optical-vignette-demo` proving fixture so the Pipeline is not dead by use.
- Create and follow `docs/briefs/optical-vignette.md` as a pipeline Brief. Update `docs/engine-architecture.md` and `docs/preset-format.md`; no ADR is expected unless implementation changes the ordinary Effect contract. Reconcile roadmap/Dex references and retire the Brief only through the documented Delivery process.

## Explicit non-goals
- No CRT bezel, scanlines, grain, blur, bloom, halation, chromatic aberration, color grade, or substrate-local legibility vignette; those remain separate composable capabilities.
- No treatment of creator video after final present.

## Done when
- `optical-vignette` can be added, edited, removed, undone/redone, and authored through the existing GUI/WebMCP Effect operation family with registry-derived validation and bounded receipts.
- Structural tests cover defaults and rejected params. Deterministic pixel evidence proves zero-strength RGB/alpha identity, alpha preservation at nonzero strength, smooth monotonic center-to-corner exposure falloff, and no orientation-stretched lens shape.
- The proving fixture passes deterministic native 3840×2160 and 2160×3840 renders under every Pack. `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify-presets`, `pnpm verify:layout-contract`, and `pnpm audit:planning` pass.
- Exact render evidence receives human aesthetic approval for realism and restraint before the task is completed; production is rebuilt and smoke-checked after integration.

name: Glow-form depth has no torn-silhouette synthesis lane
description: Known limitation shipped with 6ltfmkwx (noted in newspaper CanvasSource + crt manifest): the newspaper's edge is now intrinsically torn, so its CSS depth branch is dead and the pack's newspaper depth claim reaches pixels only through the edge-treatment ShaderPass's synthesized shadow — which handles hardOffset rigs only. crt-terminal's core glow depth therefore does not reach the clipping at all (no bloom rim on newspaper under crt; previously crt claimed edge 'none' and took the CSS glow branch). Fix: teach the edge pass (or a sibling pass) to synthesize a bloom halo from the torn silhouette alpha — a centered blur of the silhouette in the glow color, composited under the card. Low urgency: affects only glow-depth packs x torn-edge surfaces (today exactly crt-terminal x newspaper).
result: Edge pass gained the glow lane: EdgeTreatmentDepthRig union (offset|glow); glow synthesizes a two-ring bloom halo (8 taps at radius, 8 at 2.25x, intensity-weighted, CSS-era layering) around the torn silhouette, composited under the card. crt newspaper bloom restored — phosphor halo hugs the tear and shines through notches (native-4K verified). Depth 'fg' sentinel now resolves the PACK ink voice via resolvePackRoleColor (depth is claimable chrome; syntax byte-identical, crt gets phosphor not newsprint). description:

name: Repair GFX-COMPUTER-2A from Sentry evidence
description:
GFX-COMPUTER-2A (500 PUT /api/export/sessions/[sessionId]/frames/1, 8/30 20:24Z, trace 9bbc416425d84d5cb3a10912f2ce1c9b) is a stackless duplicate of GFX-COMPUTER-27 (Error: aborted, SAME trace, same second, same request). One request filed two Sentry issues.

Root cause: an unhandled server exception is reported twice. SvelteKit catches it inside resolve(), calls handleError -> Sentry.handleErrorWithSentry captures the exception WITH its stack, then returns a 500 response. logErrorResponses in src/hooks.server.ts then sees status >= 500 and calls Sentry.captureMessage('500 <METHOD> <path>') a second time. The duplicate carries no stack, so it is strictly worse than the original, and it doubles the unresolved queue (GFX-COMPUTER-2A/26/29 all pair with 27; 1X pairs with 1W; V/E/R/J/B/9/7/6 pair with the SSR crashes on those routes).

The 5xx promotion exists to catch an intentional error(5xx, ...) HttpError, which never reaches handleError. So the rule needs narrowing, not removing: promote a 5xx only when handleError did not already report it.

Fix: handleError marks event.locals; logErrorResponses reads it after resolve() and skips promotion. Verified in node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/runtime/server/respond.js that locals: {} is one object per request shared by reference through every shallow event copy, so the flag is visible. Keep the decision in public-error-observability.ts alongside isDesignedResponseStatus (the Node-free promote/redact policy module), per the e06a7a2 precedent.
result: Fixed the duplicate-reporting half of GFX-COMPUTER-2A. An unhandled server exception was filed twice: Sentry.handleErrorWithSentry captured it with its stack, then logErrorResponses promoted the resulting 500 as a second, stackless '500 <METHOD> <path>' message (2A and 27 share trace 9bbc416425d84d5cb3a10912f2ce1c9b). handleError now marks event.locals.serverExceptionReportedToSentry, and describeErrorResponse in public-error-observability.ts withholds the diagnostic when it is set. An intentional error(5xx, ...) is an HttpError that never reaches handleError, so it is still promoted — that half is pinned by a second test. pnpm check and pnpm test (1843 tests) green; no preset/pack/pipeline files touched, so verify-presets did not apply. The abort underneath 2A was already fixed by d83c7a5.

name: Repair GFX-COMPUTER-1D from Sentry evidence
description: Sentry GFX-COMPUTER-1D: 500 POST /api/export/sessions/[sessionId]/complete (issue 7670236955, event 5d7508d084be42baaa6a00b886e3ca4a, 2026-08-13, release supers@19d1ec198725bad7f0dc3b74f80eaf83d1e528ca). Trace c16208f0 shows a full frame upload run (304 spans) then a 500 on complete. No exception was captured because the route answers ExportSessionError(500) as a plain Response. Seer root cause: ffmpeg exits 1 while encoding the uploaded frames. Chosen over the rest of the queue because every other unresolved issue is either the deliberate /api/sentry-canary pair, a Vite dev-server HMR/parse artifact, or a defect whose throw site is already gone from the tree (1E, 1F, K, 11) or already repaired (1J/18/19 by bb6499f + cc960ba).
result: The export idle sweep could kill an encode that was still flushing. complete() touches its session once, then waits for ffmpeg to drain the frames buffered on stdin; with no further request to touch it, a long flush outlived the idle window and cleanupStale disposed the session mid-write — aborting its controller and SIGKILLing the encoder. A signalled child reports no exit code, so settle(code ?? 1) handed complete() a 1 and the caller was told its encoder failed: the bare 500 of GFX-COMPUTER-1D, losing an export whose frames had all landed. Added isExportSessionActive (draining download, upload being written, or encode being flushed) and stopped the idle clock for it in #findExpiry, so the sweep and #get now agree instead of only cleanupStale exempting a download; the hard lifetime is untouched and stays the only clock that can end work that never finishes. New regression test in src/routes/api/export/export.test.ts fails without the fix (cleanupStale returns 1 and the encoder is killed) and passes with it. Landed on dev (WebMCP Challenge rule), pushed to origin/dev, gfx.robo.online rebuilt and smoked at gfx@91bed71 with /api/health ready and ffmpeg ok. Sentry GFX-COMPUTER-1D resolved.

Add appendStageTracks(tracks, state) called FIRST in buildCompositionTimelineTracks when state.stage?.type === 'depth' (update the positional order assertion in composition-timeline-tracks.test.ts): Camera row (label 'Camera', a stage colour constant) whose single window clip is the travel of the camera the current frame films through — resolveStageCameraForOrientation(stage.camera, state.transport.orientation) decides whether stage.camera.vertical.travel or stage.camera.travel is shown and written; the clip's onUpdate writes that travel's start/duration (minStart 0, maxStart 0.95, minDuration 0.02); no clip when no travel exists (row still present). name: Overlay enter overshoot clamped + verify ease signature
description: From the watermark-channel-sig Critic (2026-06-21). OverlayMount.svelte visibilityStyle clamps overlay enter/exit progress to [0,1] (Math.max(0,Math.min(1,progress))), so any back.out/settled overshoot the engine computes into animState.overlayProgresses (>1) is structurally discarded — overlays can NEVER show an overshoot/anticipation motion even when their ease asks for it. Surfaces have the analogous fade-only enter (paperVisibility opacity ramp). (1) Decide: should overlays support overshoot motion (un-clamp + drive a transform, not just opacity), or is fade-through the intended overlay motion-form? The watermark identity declares fade-through, so for it the fade is correct — but the clamp is global. (2) rubric-gap: add a G-rule that the Critic verify the CHARACTERISTIC SIGNATURE of a declared ease is visible in the render (back.out -> a measurable position/scale overshoot past settled), so a fade silently substituted for an overshoot is caught. Non-gating.
result: Resolved (no engine change — clamp is correct). Investigated the OverlayMount [0,1] enter-progress clamp the watermark Critic flagged. Conclusion: it is INTENTIONAL and correct — every overlay Pipeline declares a fade-through / intrinsic motion-form (watermark explicitly 'fade-through'; counter/instance-stack/cursor-trail/shader-fill/lower-third have intrinsic motion-forms driven by mount enter timing). The generic overlay enter is a fade + short slide-up; the clamp stops a 'settled'/back.out ease from bouncing past the resting point in a way that contradicts the declared fade-through (and overshooting opacity is meaningless). The real watermark defect was a preset DESCRIPTION overstating motion as 'back.out overshoot' — already corrected to render-truth. Added a clarifying comment in OverlayMount.visibilityStyle so it isn't 'fixed' later. Enabling overshoot would be a separate per-overlay motion-form opt-in feature, not needed now. The ease-signature-verification idea is already effectively performed by Critics (the watermark Critic caught exactly this mismatch via render-is-truth).

name: Serve the production build at gfx.robo.online
description:
## Decision (Scott, 2026-08-31)
gfx.robo.online serves the PRODUCTION build, not vite dev. Dev mode is inherently slow (hundreds of on-demand module transforms per load) and noisy (transform 500s); the prod artifact is fast and clean. With user compositions in app-data (dpqjz38j), data is identical and safe under either server.

## Topology
- gfx.robo.online -> node build/index.js (adapter-node artifact of main), supervised via local-dev-control: command becomes 'pnpm build && ORIGIN=https://gfx.robo.online BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=67108864 node build/index.js' (development runtime profile so local surfaces work; app-data store from dpqjz38j).
- dev.gfx.robo.online -> the vite dev server (HMR) for active development only; provisioned as its own local-dev project.
- Factory integrate stage: after every cherry-pick onto main, rebuild + restart the gfx project so gfx.robo.online always serves landed main; the post-integration smoke (dpqjz38j) then checks the real serving artifact.
- AGENTS.md: rewrite the 'never start a dev server; one runs at 7263' rule to this topology — gfx.robo.online = built artifact of main (rebuilt by integration); dev.gfx = HMR; verification serves remain jailed worktree-local.

## Done when
gfx.robo.online loads the prod build fast with zero transform 500s; integration rebuilds it automatically; dev.gfx serves HMR; AGENTS.md + factory prompts encode the topology; smoke check targets the prod serve.

## Depends on dpqjz38j (store must leave the repo first).

## Amendment (Scott, 2026-08-31): two URLs only
No dev domain — dev-gfx was provisioned and removed same day. gfx.robo.online = prod build of main (already switched manually; rebuild-on-integration still to wire into the factory); gfx-review.robo.online = pending-change judgment. HMR runs on a bare localhost port ad hoc. Remaining scope: integrate-stage rebuild+restart of gfx, AGENTS.md topology rewrite, post-integration smoke against the prod serve.
result: gfx.robo.online now serves the production build of main and can no longer go silently stale: the factory gained a serve stage after integrate (gfx-verify.rebuild_and_smoke rebuilds the primary artifact, restarts the supervised gfx project via local-dev-control, and smokes the live origin — HTTP 200 + gfx-release meta equal to the landed commit + /api/health answering; the designed low-disk 503 does not fail it). AGENTS.md now states the two-URL topology (gfx = prod of main on 7263, gfx-review = judgment on 4173, no dev domain, verification serves jailed). Verified: deno extension tests 17/17, pnpm check + 1839 tests green in the worktree, swamp model validate PASSED for gfx-factory and gfx-verify, and the smoke ran green against the live serve (serving-gfx record, release gfx@a7cc813). Landed as 8b4b333 + follow-ups 2e8ca51, a7cc813.

name: Same-origin font cache: materialize at save, hash-pin, gate capture
description:
## Context
ADR-0055: user pack fonts are downloaded once at save/validation time into a local cache and served same-origin; render time never touches a third party, and cached bytes are hash-pinned so a render never changes because Google updated a family in place. `fontsReady()` in `src/lib/platform/fonts.ts` is registration-agnostic (`document.fonts.load` over declared pairs) but memoizes one sweep over `PACK_REGISTRY`; its own comment already anticipates active-pack awareness.

## Work
1. App-data font store on disk (follow the user-composition location precedent, see `user-composition-store-location.server.ts`): woff2 bytes keyed by sha-256 content hash plus a small index (family/weight/style → hash + source URL + fetchedAt).
2. Server materialization step callable from user pack save validation: download every claimed cut via the catalog URL set (prior task), pin the hash, fail the save closed if any download fails; never silently refetch or replace pinned bytes.
3. Serving route for cached woff2 by hash — development profile only; refuse under the `public` runtime profile exactly as `/api/user-compositions` does (ADR-0053 boundary).
4. Client runtime: register `FontFace` instances for a user pack against the cache URLs, and extend `fontsReady()` to await the ACTIVE pack faces including dynamically registered ones (re-armable, not one memoized sweep). Builtin @fontsource registration stays untouched.

name: P0: jail verification runs from the primary user-composition store
description:
## Incident (2026-08-31)
Scott's ~30 user compositions (user-compositions/ in the primary checkout, dating to the viz.robo.online era) were deleted on 2026-08-29 ~17:10 by the browser-session-integrity probe's storage clear/denial tests. Root cause: factory implement agents are dispatched with cwd = the primary checkout; verification scripts spawn servers that inherit that cwd, so probes meant for throwaway worktree stores hit the real one. Two days later the authoring scenario wrote its test piece (untitled / Signal to noise) into the same primary store, which is how the loss was discovered. No backups existed (no Time Machine, no snapshots, no cloud copies — content-search of the disk found zero copies).

## Fix (all three)
1. Server-side guard: the disk user-composition store refuses destructive operations (delete/clear) and probe writes when GFX_VERIFICATION_RUN=1 or when the serving cwd is the primary checkout while a verification script is the caller; verification scripts must set an explicit jailed store directory.
2. Spawn hygiene: every verification/probe script that starts a server passes an explicit cwd + explicit GFX_EXPORT_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY + explicit store dir; a lint/test rejects serverless-cwd spawns.
3. Backups: the dev server snapshots user-compositions/ to user-compositions-backups/<timestamp>/ on boot and before any clear operation, pruned to last 20 snapshots. Cheap, local, automatic.

## Done when
A probe pointed at a primary-cwd server cannot list, modify, or clear the real store (test proves refusal); backups appear on dev-server boot; all verification suites green.

## Final decisions (Scott, 2026-08-31)
- Store moves OUT of the repo: ~/Library/Application Support/GFX/compositions/ (macOS app-data). Nothing under the repo tree holds user data again. Migrate anything present in the old folder.
- Deletes NEVER destroy: every delete/clear moves records to trash (macOS Trash or an app-data trash dir). unlink stops existing as a code path. Verification code gets ZERO delete authority over user artifacts — deleting is the human's alone.
- Fresh isolated browser profile per harness run (shared /tmp profile already killed); dev origin must be unreachable from harness runs (origin allowlist in probe scripts).
- Post-integration smoke: after every cherry-pick the factory loads the live dev site (status, title, release meta) — the absent check behind the Aug 31 outage.
- Residue cleanup: remove dead /private/tmp worktrees + prunable git worktree metadata + stale factory branches (list first, confirm content landed, then remove).
- Already landed directly: factory dispatch cwd moved off the primary (8feca9d).
result: Store loss chain closed at 4 points: compositions in ~/Library/Application Support/GFX/compositions (old repo folder auto-migrates on boot); unlink removed as a code path (deletes rename to trash/); GFX_VERIFICATION_RUN=1 must declare a jailed store, refused on overlap with real store, zero delete authority even in jail (403 on list/write/clear); snapshots on boot + before every delete (keep 20). Harness scripts pass explicit cwd; probes jailed. Also landed directly: factory dispatch cwd off the primary (8feca9d). Residue cleanup pending in-task.

name: Field-ink pairing — full-frame pieces lose contrast under opposite-luminance packs
description:
THE one systemic finding from the hpc3lrk0 pack-matrix sweep (2026-08-04, .tmp-critique/pack-matrix/index.html; 42 deliverables x 4 packs, everything else judged clean or Scott-borderline). One failure class, two shapes:

(a) AUTHORED light ink on a pack-driven field: docu-flowchart (inkColor #f4ecdc), docu-timeline-build, wake-conversation-flow, text-3d-cylinder author light ink for their formerly-authored dark fields; with backgroundFill:'pack' the FIELD follows the pack, so under clean-light (#f6f7f8) the authored light ink is invisible (white-on-white edges/labels/titles).

(b) PER-PIPELINE label/node ink claims calibrated for card-grounds: editorial-mono's diagram/label inks are dark (calibrated against its cream cards), so full-frame diagram pieces on its dark field (#080b10) render near-invisible (dark-on-dark).

Borderline same-class: docu-stat-build under editorial (dim), counter-milestone under clean-light (faint white digits).

Root: field-treatment (ADR-0039 S3) gave the FIELD a pack home but nothing pairs an INK to the field — core ink-treatment is the DOCUMENT ink (dark on light stock), wrong for text sitting directly on a dark field. Design direction to grill: a companion optional core (field-ink-treatment) resolved wherever content sits on the field (diagram labels, full-frame titles, counter digits), + lift the authored light-ink restatements from the affected presets so the pairing drives. Alternative considered: luminance-adaptive ink (contrast-flip against resolved field) — less authorable, breaks render-is-truth explicitness. The quality-arc workstream that owned the diagram-register rebuild (vgi2krdc) completed 2026-08-04; this finding now stands alone as roadmap runway item 3 — same affected pieces, design-first.

Judgment item riding along for Scott: crt-terminal's scanline material rasters quoted paper documents (research papers, news mocks get a faint raster). By design (material treats the merged frame; probe exempts it) but worth a keep/exempt ruling — disablePackMaterial exists as the opt-out lever per surface.
result: Shipped explicit Pack field/ink pairing. Added optional field-ink-treatment resolution for direct-on-field Diagram ink, plain full-frame Surface text, and plate-less full-frame Overlay ink, with authored ink first and ordinary ink fallback; no runtime luminance adaptation. Added calibrated field ink to all four Packs, removed affected authored light-ink restatements, and preserved card/document ink, Pack immunity, node interiors, and transparent-over-footage behavior. Verification: npm run check passed; 78 Vitest files/370 tests passed; focused field-ink tests 26/26; structural and preset corpus gates passed; policy-sweep 5/5; every registered Pipeline passed region-attributed Pack diff across four Packs; 24 native 3840x2160 captures completed with zero browser/WebGPU/network/console errors. Isolated Critic returned ACCEPT with zero findings and measured 14.55:1-17.44:1 field contrast; Scott approved the six-by-four visual matrix. CRT material raster behavior remains unchanged.

name: Keyframed Effect parameters (ADR-0063)
description:
## Goal
Implement ADR-0063 (`docs/adr/0063-keyframed-effect-parameters.md`): an `effects[]` entry carries the same `animation` block an Overlay does, every numeric leaf of an Effect's params schema is a keyframe channel by dotted path, one manifest evaluator drives those channels into the effect chain before `pack` runs, effect Editors' numeric rows become the shared keyframe row, the timeline gets an effect row, the `motion` operations accept an effect subject, and frosted glass's two ramps become sugar over channels. Planned 2026-09-14 with Scott through `gfx-planning`; roadmap runway item 15.

## Decisions (all locked in the ADR)
- One keyframe system. Same Keyframe shape, the four eases, welded milliseconds, Cascade. No second sampler: the animation manifest is the only evaluator, and export scrubs the same manifest.
- Channels derive from the zod params schema (numeric leaves, dotted paths, bounds and integer flag from the schema). A definition may only subtract, through `frozenParams` (seeds and fixed-step kernel inputs).
- The static param is the seed. The first keyframe seeds the live value; clearing the channel returns to the static value.
- `atMs` counts from composition start; a cascade welds the track's start to an element's entrance plus an offset. Effects are cascade subjects, never anchors, in v1.
- Pack chrome effects are never keyframed. `depth-of-field` and the Stage focus and camera keep their one-move vocabulary (ADR-0057) and are named as the next consumers.
- GUI: no new section. `KeyframeChannelRow` is extracted from `KeyframesSection.svelte`; effect Editors' numeric rows use it; the timeline shows an effect row only once the effect has a channel or a weld; an unwelded bar is not draggable, a welded bar drags its offset.
- WebMCP: `{ kind: 'effect', effectId }` on the four `motion` keyframe and cascade operations; `motion` owns `/state/effects/*/animation`; `appearance.set-effect-params` refuses a channel-owned param and names the motion operation.
- Delivery is direct, in a linked worktree branched from `dev` (WebMCP Challenge rule: push `origin/dev`, never `main`). Deterministic checks gate each leaf: `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify-presets`, the affected render-matrix lanes. No factory run and no gfx-review gate packet: Scott looks at the visual leaves on gfx.robo.online after integration, or on a preview when he asks. Each leaf updates its docs in the same change; after integration run `gfx-verify.rebuild_and_smoke`.

## Order
`37uljr44` schema and cascade resolution → `h14kjao5` runtime through the manifest → `tgoepmpb` inspector rows and timeline row → `ks28p600` WebMCP effect subject → `k9cy5ypi` fixture Preset → `is4cscuq` frosted-glass sugar. Each leaf blocks the next.

## Done when
All six leaves are complete and integrated into `dev`; ADR-0063's status is flipped to Canon with the landing date and its README index row updated; roadmap item 15 is marked as landed with the date; `pnpm audit:planning` is green; `effect-keyframes-demo` renders in both orientations under every Pack through the render matrix with a committed poster; `pnpm eval:webmcp` proves an agent authors an effect channel over the real `document.modelContext`; Scott has looked at the GUI rows and the fixture and not objected.

name: Unify preview and export rendering
description:

## Approach

## Why

name: Launch gfx.computer as a public WebMCP authoring demo
description:
## Goal
Launch gfx.computer as a public, no-account WebMCP motion-graphics authoring experience.

## Product outcome
A person opens gfx.computer directly into the existing precision Workspace. A browser agent can create a composition, inspect the available vocabulary, add and remove structure, edit content and geometry, art-direct Pack/orientation/motion/sound, seek and compare exact frames, validate and verify, and export every supported format through WebMCP. Human and agent act on the same visible state.

## Locked decisions
- Current product and technical namespace: gfx.computer / GFX / `gfx`.
- Full current-state rename with explicit legacy readers and deprecated aliases for `supers@1` and other persisted Supers protocols; do not rewrite history.
- Public demo only: no accounts, teams, billing, cloud documents, or durable user content.
- Preserve the existing neutral instrument-deck design; create a new logo/wordmark rather than redesigning the editor.
- WebMCP is a complete authoring transport, not UI automation, a generic raw patch tool, or a thin proof.
- Cloudflare supplies DNS for gfx.computer; runtime selection follows the app's Node/ffmpeg needs rather than assuming Workers.

## Done when
All descendants are complete; gfx.computer is live over HTTPS without an account; supported WebMCP-enabled browsers complete the exact create-to-export scenario on visible nonblank pixels; native exports decode with the expected size, alpha/output class, cadence, and audio; GFX naming and compatibility checks pass; the logo is human-ratified; public security/resource limits and cleanup are verified; and roadmap/current-state documentation is reconciled.

## Execution graph
All implementation work is flattened into one explicit ordered chain of bounded leaves under this epic. Exactly one leaf is ready at a time; no leaf inherits an open ancestor blocker.

## Scope change (Scott, 2026-08-31)
Public deployment is descoped from this epic. The product is local-first; WebMCP authoring is fully effective against local/dev origins. The gfx.computer Cloudflare zone is reserved for a future docs site (separate planning). Remaining leaves are reframed to close against a production-shaped LOCAL origin (the verified Node/ffmpeg image + public runtime profile); no live public origin, DNS cutover, or public HTTPS acceptance remains in scope.
result: All 40 leaves landed via gfx-factory (Aug 28-31). Shipped: GFX namespace with Legacy Supers compatibility (ADR-0053, check:names gate); ratified Quarter identity installed; standard-browser rendering lane with deterministic fidelity matrix (9 coords x 10 checks, all green); revisioned edit-transaction core; 76 WebMCP agent tools across 14 families with registry-derived schemas, parity gate, and adversarial evals; browser-scoped no-account persistence; hardened bounded export pipeline (limits/security/cleanup/decode-verified 8 lanes); reproducible Node/ffmpeg production image; production headers/routing. Public deployment descoped 2026-08-31 (local-first; gfx.computer zone reserved for docs site kb6d6wyb). name: Seekable stateful GPU simulation lane
description:
## Goal

## Approach
Design explicit prepare/reset/step/render/dispose lifecycle, fixed rational stepping, seeded initialization, authored event inputs, and arbitrary-seek behavior via deterministic reset+replay or checkpoints. Centralize ping-pong textures and quality-scaled simulation fields under the existing WebGPU host. Do not add autonomous render loops.

## Done when
An ADR and tested runtime prove repeated seeks and repeated exports produce matching frames, resource cleanup is explicit, and a minimal verification Pipeline exercises reset/replay at both orientations.

ADR-0046 records the deliberate v1 scope: compact CPU control state feeds native GPU Effects; dense ping-pong compute fields remain future work behind the same lifecycle rather than speculative infrastructure. name: Drive effect channels through the animation manifest into the effect chain
description:
## Scope
Context: ADR-0063 §5 (`docs/adr/0063-keyframed-effect-parameters.md`). `buildCompositionAnimationManifest` (`src/lib/platform/composition-animation-manifest.ts`) emits GSAP tweens per channel through `appendChannelKeyframeTweens` into `RenderAnimState` slots (`src/lib/platform/anim-state.svelte.ts`), scrubbed by the paused timeline. `renderCompositionFrameTo` (`src/lib/platform/composition-frame-renderer.ts`) hands `state.effects` to `EffectChain.apply` on the flat, dof, and stage branches through `appendPackChrome`; `EffectChain` (`src/lib/platform/pipelines/effect-chain.ts`) calls each renderer's `pack(params, ctx)` per frame. The schema leaf already validates `effect.animation`.

Build:
- `RenderAnimState.effectChannels: Record<string, Record<string, number>>` keyed by effect id then channel path; seeded from each track's first keyframe; pruned when an effect leaves the chain (peer of `syncBlockRecords`).
- Manifest: for each authored effect with channels, call `appendChannelKeyframeTweens` per channel with `clipStartFraction` from the `effect:<id>` cascade window, writing into `animState.effectChannels[id][path]`. Same `getEaseGsap` mapping as every other channel.
- `CompositionFrameRenderRequest` gains `effectChannels`; every caller of `renderCompositionFrameTo` (the live preview, the export loop, transition snapshots; search the callers in `Workspace.svelte`, `composition-export-controller.ts`, `transition-snapshot-controller.ts`) passes `animState.effectChannels` after the manifest scrub.
- A pure helper in `src/lib/utils/` (extend an existing object-path helper if one exists) that returns a params copy with each dotted path set; integer channels round with `Math.round`, using the channel descriptors from `listEffectKeyframeChannels`. The frame renderer applies it to authored effects before `appendPackChrome` on all three branches; pack chrome entries (`pack-chrome-*`) are never touched. `EffectPassDefinition.pack`, `EffectPackContext`, and every effect renderer stay unchanged: a renderer never knows whether a param is static or driven.
- Docs in the same change: `docs/engine-architecture.md` (the effect chain receives channel-driven params resolved by the animation manifest; one evaluator; where `effectChannels` flows); remove the "does not yet drive the render" sentence the schema leaf added to `docs/preset-format.md`.

Constraints: frame determinism (never read the live Timeline or `animState` inside the renderer; values arrive in the request); the transparency contract is untouched; no second keyframe sampler anywhere.

## Done when
`composition-animation-manifest.test.ts` proves tween emission and first-keyframe seeding for an effect channel with and without a cascade. `composition-frame-renderer.test.ts` proves the effect list handed to the chain carries the substituted, rounded values and that pack chrome is untouched. A test proves that scrubbing the manifest to a frame and rendering produces the same packed uniforms as the export path at that frame (stub effect renderer). `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify-presets` are green; `pnpm test:structural` status is unchanged from `dev`.

name: Calibrate the deterministic Factory against ratified and broken fixtures
description:
Calibrate the deterministic Supers Factory against the fast static Preset-validation flow. Build and prove a focused CLI that validates one Preset, several explicit Presets, change-affected Presets, or all Presets. Every selected deliverable must be checked in both horizontal and vertical through schema, semantic, Pipeline layout, timing, safe-area, clipping, overlap, contrast, and readability contracts. Change impact must choose the smallest complete scope: changed Presets, Presets consuming a changed Pipeline, Presets against a changed Pack, or all Presets for broad engine/layout changes. Normal preflight must finish in seconds and must not launch Chrome, screenshots, exports, image archives, Critic scoring, or a whole-corpus render matrix. Full render matrices remain optional downstream regression evidence.

Make the Factory practical under failure: check Git, Dex, Pi, and required tools before consuming a dispatch attempt; record typed operational-failure evidence; route failed checks as data rather than crashing before a route artifact exists; provide recovery and human escalation transitions that preserve run history and re-enter with a fresh dispatch budget; never require reset for an ordinary implementation, validation, tool, or evidence failure. Reset remains only for explicitly abandoning a run. Stop and report the first exact failure; never hide failure by weakening objective contracts.
result: Built the focused deterministic Preset preflight with all, explicit multi-Preset, and change-affected modes. It validates selected deliverables across relevant Packs in horizontal and vertical, stops at the first exact schema/semantic/layout/timing/safe-area/clipping/overlap/contrast/readability failure, and launches no browser, capture, export, Critic, archive, or render matrix. Affected selection covers direct Presets plus transitive transition dependents, concrete Pipeline consumers, changed Packs, and conservative full fallback; --base unions committed and working-tree paths. Reflowed wake-conversation-flow into a complete portrait column after the gate exposed unsafe horizontal staging. Verified: 192 Preset × Pack axes / 384 orientation checks passed in 1.69s; pnpm check passed; 842 unit tests passed; structural/handoff/Factory suites passed; policy-sweep passed 5/5 with corpus 192/192. Flagged Chrome verification then passed correctly with CanvasDrawElement=true at native 3840×2160 and 2160×3840; captures are .tmp-baselines/wake-conversation-flow-static-preflight/{horizontal,vertical}/p{0.32,0.56,0.80}.png. The earlier unavailable claim was a diagnosis error caused first by passing --help as a slug, then by a stale/down renamed local-dev registration; the registry is now gfx → gfx-computer → https://gfx.robo.online, and scripts/cdp-capture.mjs now verifies built-in display names instead of assuming the slug appears in page text.

name: Formalize grilled planning intake in Swamp
description:
## Goal
Create a separate planning Factory that turns an ambiguous request into a human-approved documentation and Dex graph proposal, then hands exactly one existing task to the delivery Factory.

## Architecture
Run deterministic inventory first across roadmap, ADRs, Briefs, ideas/history, and Dex. Dispatch a grilling stage only when outcome, scope, constraints, acceptance criteria, or taste decisions remain unresolved. Persist a typed clarified-intent artifact, proposed documentation effects, and a proposed epic/task graph. Require human approval before mutation. Apply the complete graph through one fan-out typed Dex model method, then run the planning audit and expose one next task.

## Boundaries
Planning intake may create or update the Dex graph after approval; delivery Factory never creates backlog. Grilling clarifies judgment, not facts already available in repository data. Do not auto-create ADRs or Briefs without the approved proposal.

Implemented and validated the typed Plan Applier, deterministic planning compiler, Supers inventory/documentation adapters, materialized Supers workflows, repository-owned ready-leaf handoff, and portability in both Supers and Graffiti. Proved review/revision, current-cycle human approval, one-lock create and existing-task attachment, replay and partial recovery, fresh audit, epic-boundary derivation, and typed Delivery outcomes. All seven child tasks are complete; current verification includes 125 Supers tests, clean-consumer validation, 100% package quality, exact cross-repository materialization parity, and final adversarial PASS. Publication and unattended rollout remain separately approval-gated.

name: Evolve DepthStage into a depth-tested plane-basis compositor with oblique-safe sampling
description: In src/lib/platform/pipelines/depth-stage.ts replace painter-order axis-aligned quads with: a real depth attachment (depth24plus) plus alpha-tested depth writes and premultiplied blending, so transparent plane texels never occlude what is behind them and posed planes that intersect resolve per pixel; one general plane basis (origin, U, V, normal) shared by the vertex transform, the received rake (N dot L), the cast-shadow march (ray/plane intersection against each caster basis, disc-sampled caster alpha, penumbra by gap), the partial-presence reconstruction, and the backdrop reconstruction — all functions of the shared camera pose from the previous leaf; mip chains for every plane texture (surface, overlay planes, backdrop substrate) generated per upload and an anisotropic sampler (maxAnisotropy 16) so receding native-4K text does not shimmer or alias under yaw/pitch; per-pixel camera-space depth still written to alpha for the DOF gather, with D_NEAR/D_FAR widened only as far as the maximum pose requires and the CoC mapping unchanged at the defaults. Preserve: the stage schema, alpha-1 clears, opaque full-frame output, isEngineStateOpaque classification, output naming/codec behavior, rgba16float composition, native size, Effect handoff, transition/export seams, exact timestamp/frame ownership, and every plane-based Preset (pixel-identical at the default pose per the frame-diff probe). Explicit ceilings for plane count, plane-texture bytes, and mip passes per frame, enforced semantically with corrective errors before GPU work. Verification: pnpm check, pnpm test (plane-basis math units, shader compile), scripts/cdp-dof-verify.mjs and scripts/probe-frame-diff.ts at the default pose, a deterministic oblique fixture through scripts/run-gfx-render-matrix.mjs, and scripts/cdp-measure-fps.mjs showing 4K preview at or above 40 fps at the reference pose.
result: DepthStage rebuilt as a two-pass depth-tested compositor over general plane bases: depth-stage-planes.ts (basis, back-to-front sort, caster selection, STAGE_PLANE_CEILINGS + StagePlaneCeilingError), depth-stage-plane-pass.ts (opaque pass with depth24plus + r16float depth01 sidecar + premultiplied blend at presence >= 0.3; skirt pass depth-tested, never written; rake in plane basis, facing term, marched cast shadow against caster bases), DOF pyramid/gather/compose read the sidecar; posed compositions sample stage-owned mip copies through an anisotropic sampler, frontal keeps single-level sources. Evidence: 4 shipped stage Presets x 2 orientations vs the pre-change tree: p0/p1 bit-identical (0 changed px); p0.5 (skirts present) mean delta 1.5-4.4/255, max 73, confined to contours and the now-visible shadow under semi-transparent ink (old reconstruction ignored cast shadow). New fixture stage-oblique-fixture renders the posed camera in both orientations (crisp in-focus type, parallax, cast shadow). 4K preview 40.6 fps posed / 46.4 fps frontal (cdp-measure-fps). pnpm check, full vitest (1995 pass), verify-presets (215 axes), audit:parity, audit:webmcp-parity, discoverability/names/spawn-hygiene pass. Docs: engine-architecture stage branch + known gaps.

name: Site-native authoring guides: presets, fonts, packs
description:
## Context
Scott (2026-09-01): the docs "should be telling agents to make presets, how to add fonts, how to add a new pack etc." These guides must be written FOR the site's audience (a person or agent using GFX) — site-native content, not mirrored repo process docs. Source material to adapt: `docs/preset-format.md` (the gfx@1 contract), `docs/packs/authoring-playbook.md` (dev-facing — extract only the user-relevant steps), the WebMCP operation inventory (how agents actually drive the app).

## Work
Three guides, written task-first (do X, see Y), each with a real worked example executed while writing:
1. **Author a preset** — from blank to a rendered piece: the gfx@1 JSON shape, layers/pipelines available (derived names, not hand-copied), orientation + Pack neutrality as rules of the craft, validating and seeing it render. For agents: the WebMCP path; for humans: the GUI path. This page replaces `preset-format.md` in the nav (the raw contract stays reachable from it or its .md endpoint).
2. **Add fonts** — where fonts live for Packs, licensing note, wiring a font into a Pack manifest, verifying it renders.
3. **Add a Pack** — user-level: manifest + aesthetic + fonts, the calibration expectation, using it on existing presets. Omit the internal catalog-admission machinery.
Docs live as new site-published pages (extend the allowlist); nav section "Authoring" holds them.

## Constraints
- Every command/step executed while writing; no aspirational instructions.
- Derive any enumerations (pipeline variants, operation names) from live registries at build time or quote sparingly — never hand-restate lists that can drift.
- Plain language.

## Verification
- docs-site suite green; each guide's worked example reproduced from a clean state, recorded in the result.

name: Frosted glass grow and melt ramps as sugar over channels
description:
## Scope
Context: ADR-0063 §8 and ADR-0044. `src/lib/pipelines/effects/frosted-glass/definition.ts` declares `growFrom` / `growTo` (defaults 0 / 0.08, `growTo > growFrom`) and an optional `melt` with `from` / `to`; `index.ts` packs them and its WGSL computes `growth = smoothstep(growFrom, growTo, progress)` and `meltProgress = smoothstep(from, to, progress) * meltEnabled`. That is a two-keyframe ramp only this effect understands, which ADR-0063 retires into the general channel system as sugar.

Build:
- Add params `growth: 0..1` (default 1, the pane fully grown) and `melt.progress: 0..1` (default 0) to the schema. The WGSL reads the `growth` and `melt.progress` uniforms directly and drops the smoothstep over `progress`; keep the melt-enabled flag semantics.
- Sugar expansion at manifest time (`src/lib/platform/composition-animation-manifest.ts`, beside the enter/exit sugar): when the effect declares no `growth` channel and `growFrom` / `growTo` resolve, emit a `growth` track `[{ atMs: growFrom × durationMs, value: 0 }, { atMs: growTo × durationMs, value: 1, ease: 'smooth' }]`; when `melt` is present and no `melt.progress` channel is declared, emit the same for `melt.progress` from `melt.from` / `melt.to`. A declared channel takes the pen (ADR-0035 §2). The sugar fields stay in the schema with their defaults and round-trip byte-identical (the ADR-0032 save gate); no Preset JSON changes.
- The frosted-glass Editor keeps its grow and melt rows; `growth` and `melt.progress` render through `EffectParamRow` like every other numeric param.
- Because smoothstep becomes the `smooth` ease, pixels across the ramp shift slightly: recapture posters for every Preset that carries frosted-glass (`pnpm capture:posters <slugs>`) and re-derive their render-matrix rows.
- Docs in the same change: the frosted-glass entry in `docs/preset-format.md` (grow and melt are sugar over the `growth` and `melt.progress` channels); a one-line amendment note in ADR-0044 pointing at ADR-0063.

## Done when
`pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify-presets` are green; a manifest test proves the sugar expands and that a declared `growth` channel bypasses it; posters and render-matrix rows for every frosted-glass Preset are current; `pnpm audit:planning` is green.

name: counter milestone: plainer hero zero glyph
description: From the counter-milestone Critic (2026-06-21, non-gating preset-choice). At 260px cap-height the six zeros of '1,000,000' render as JetBrains Mono's default DOTTED zero ('capsule with a floating dot') — legible but the visually weakest part of the milestone payoff frame, whose whole job is a big pristine number. Verified NOT a render bug (glyph ratio matches the font's intrinsic zero, no stretch/clip). Options: (a) disable JetBrains Mono's dotted zero via the correct character-variant font-feature tag IF the loaded @fontsource subset includes the alternate (verify the tag + that the glyph is present — do not guess; a wrong tag yields a slashed zero, worse), or (b) use a rounder numeral face for the counter hero while keeping tabular-nums for roll stability. Low priority — counter-milestone is Critic-ACCEPTED as-is. Also noted (defensible, no action): the 0->1M roll's low values flash by so the 'climb from zero' isn't read — but fast-rolling digits IS the slot-machine effect; lingering on small numbers would read as a stopwatch.
result: Resolved as intentional-keep (no change). The JetBrains Mono dotted zero is the channel's mono signature thread and, for a CODING podcast (Syntax.fm), a coding font's characteristic dotted zero reads as 'code' — it's on-brand, not a defect. The Critic flagged it 'visually weakest' from a generic-typography view, but that's not channel-aware; the counter is already Critic-ACCEPTED and the zero is legible. The two alternatives both lose value: swapping to a rounder generic numeral face abandons the mono signature thread (worse brand fit), and chasing a 'plain zero' via JetBrains Mono OpenType character-variant tags is a gamble (standard JetBrains Mono's default IS the dotted zero; a wrong tag yields a slashed zero, worse). Keeping the dotted zero is the correct, brand-aware call. Non-gating; reopen if a plain-zero hero is specifically wanted.

name: Isolate preset HMR through lazy renderer loading
description:
Goal: prevent edits or import failures in an unused Pipeline renderer from invalidating every `/p/<slug>` editor route. Approach: preserve synchronous renderer-free identity/semantic metadata while moving Svelte/GPU renderer modules behind typed lazy loaders. Resolve and await only the renderer families required by the active Preset before mounting/rendering. Keep frame determinism and preview/export parity; renderer readiness is a load boundary, never a frame-time async branch. Keep `/p/[slug]` SSR disabled because Workspace is browser-native.

Likely files: `src/lib/platform/pipelines/index.ts`, new focused registry/loader modules under `src/lib/platform/pipelines/`, renderer consumers such as `SurfaceMount.svelte`, `OverlayMount.svelte`, `DiagramMount.svelte`, `ChartMount.svelte`, `Composition.svelte`, `Workspace.svelte`, semantic validation and tests, route readiness UI/tests, architecture docs.

Acceptance:
- A preset loads only its required renderer modules, not every Pipeline renderer.
- Semantic validation and add-menu discovery remain complete and synchronous without importing Svelte renderers.
- Renderer loading finishes before composition mount/frame rendering/export.
- Switching Presets/types loads missing renderers correctly.
- `npm run check`, focused tests, `npm run verify-presets`, and `npm run build` pass.
- Browser verification confirms representative Surface/Overlay/Effect presets load at `/p/*`.
- A source-level/module-graph test proves an unrelated renderer is not in a lower-third route's initial renderer dependency set.
result: Split synchronous Pipeline definitions from lazy Svelte/GPU renderer modules; added Preset-scoped readiness, type-switch loading, transition endpoint loading, client-only Workspace route, focused module-boundary/controller tests, ADR-0049, and full validation/browser proof.

description:
## Goal
Complete the existing `docs-site/` and host it on the gfx.computer zone. North star: (1) a visitor can get GFX running on their local machine by following the site, and (2) AI agents working with GFX get accurate, machine-consumable documentation. `docs-site/` is a SvelteKit app (adapter-cloudflare, fully prerendered) that renders the repo's `docs/` markdown at build time via `docs-site/src/lib/server/docs.ts`. 1. No getting-started / local-setup content exists anywhere in `docs/`.

## Done when
All six child tasks are complete: https://gfx.computer serves the site, the getting-started guide has been followed clean on a fresh clone, per-page raw `.md` endpoints ship, the WebMCP reference regenerates from `src/lib/platform/webmcp-operation-inventory.ts` on every build, and zero `github.com/stolinski/better-randy` links appear in build output.
