name: WebMCP: the effect subject on the motion keyframe and cascade operations
description:
## Scope
Context: ADR-0063 §10 and ADR-0054. `src/lib/platform/composition-keyframe-cascade-operations.ts` defines `CompositionKeyframeSubject`, `CompositionCascadeSubject`, and the four `motion.set-keyframe-channel` / `motion.clear-keyframe-channel` / `motion.set-cascade-anchor` / `motion.clear-cascade-anchor` operations; `src/lib/platform/webmcp-motion-tools.ts` registers them; `src/lib/platform/webmcp-operation-inventory.ts` holds the rows and each family's `ownedPaths` (`appearance` owns `/state/effects/*/params`; `motion` owns every `animation` pointer); `src/lib/platform/webmcp-tool-preconditions.ts` computes `keyframe-channel-present` and `cascade-anchor-present`; the vocabulary read row (summary "List the registered Surface, Block, Annotation, Overlay, Effect, transition, text-animation, Pack, Starter, and sound vocabulary") lists Effect types.

Build:
- Both subject types gain `{ kind: 'effect'; effectId: string }` and both kind lists include `'effect'`. `findKeyframeOwner` returns `listEffectKeyframeChannels(definition)` names for an effect; `writeElementMotion` and `writeSubjectCascade` write `effect.animation`; refusals name the effect and list its channels or the chain's effect ids; `collectCascadeEdges` and `listCompositionCascadeAnchorKeys` stay anchor-only for effects (subjects, never anchors); focus resolves to `{ target: 'effect', effectId }`.
- Inventory: the four motion rows add `/state/effects/*/animation` to `writes` and `effect` to `focus`; the `motion` family's `ownedPaths` adds `/state/effects/*/animation`. `appearance.set-effect-params` refuses a write that touches a channel-owned param (`precondition_unmet`, alternatives `motion.set-keyframe-channel` and `motion.clear-keyframe-channel`) so the agent matches the GUI, where a channel-owned param is edited only through its keyframe row. The vocabulary read lists each Effect's channels as `{ path, min, max, integer }` from `listEffectKeyframeChannels`.
- Tool input schemas in `webmcp-motion-tools.ts` derive the subject enum from the live subject-kind lists; preconditions count effect channels and welds.
- Docs in the same change: ADR-0054 wherever it enumerates keyframe subjects; `docs/preset-format.md` or `docs/user-composition-workflows.md` wherever the motion operations are documented.

Constraints: every enum derived from the live lists, never restated; no tool that clicks or patches JSON pointers; receipts stay bounded; families keep disjoint ownership.

## Done when
`composition-keyframe-cascade-operations.test.ts` covers set and clear channel and set and clear cascade on an effect, the frozen-channel refusal, the unknown-effect refusal, and the `appearance.set-effect-params` refusal on a channel-owned param. `webmcp-operation-inventory.test.ts` is green with disjoint family ownership. `webmcp-agent-selection-evals.test.ts` gains prompts such as "make the pixelation resolve as the title lands" and "slide the lens across the frame over two seconds" that select `gfx_motion_set_keyframe_channel` with an effect subject; `webmcp-agent-safety-evals.test.ts` stays green. `pnpm eval:webmcp` passes against the real `document.modelContext` (Chrome for Testing 153 at `/private/tmp/chrome-for-testing-153`, custom CDP ports, a serve with `GFX_USER_COMPOSITION_STORE_DIRECTORY` set and no `GFX_VERIFICATION_RUN`, never against gfx.robo.online). `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` are green.

name: Emit Factory effectiveness through Sentry Application Metrics
description:
## Goal
Send bounded, deterministic Factory flow measurements to one dedicated Sentry Application Metrics project so effectiveness trends compare repositories and Factory profiles beside their operational telemetry.

## Current capability
The repo uses @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0; Application Metrics are supported from 10.25.0. The canonical source remains @mgreten/software-factory-flow-metrics output.

## Architecture
No local or registry Swamp Sentry model existed as of 2026-08-05. Do not emit network side effects from a report and do not wrap the Sentry CLI in command/shell. Build a typed emitter model using the Sentry SDK and a vault-backed DSN for a dedicated Factory-observability Sentry project. It accepts only the bounded terminal-run payload, emits metrics, flushes before exit, and records a versioned success/failure result. Sentry is a trend surface, never a Factory gate.

## Comparison dimensions
Every metric carries factory.project (explicit stable project slug, never an absolute path), factory.name (local instance), factory.profile (reusable profile name/version), and factory.definition_version. Never emit work item ids, paths, actors, repo URLs, or other unbounded identifiers.

## Metric contract
- factory.run.completed count with outcome/project/factory/profile/definition/first-pass/visual attributes.
- factory.run.duration and factory.stage.duration distributions in milliseconds.
- factory.run.dispatch_attempts, factory.run.human_decisions, and factory.run.patch_cycles distributions.
- factory.run.cleanup_failure count only for cleanup-required outcomes.
- factory.metric.coverage gauge for bounded unavailable/available facts.

## Done when
The emitter model is schema-validated and fixture-tested, one terminal Factory summary produces queryable Sentry metrics and a versioned Swamp emission result, dashboards can group and compare by project/factory/profile, missing DSN is explicit/non-gating, duplicate emission is idempotent, and docs/project-control-plane.md remains accurate.
result:
Shipped and live-verified terminal-only, non-gating Factory effectiveness emission to the dedicated Sentry project scott-tolinski-projects/factory-observability. Canonical flow reports map into the bounded metric vocabulary with project/factory/profile/definition dimensions; unavailable facts remain explicit; done, cleanup-required, parked, and aborted outcomes are covered; receipts are versioned and secret-free; active runs skip emission; missing DSN remains non-gating; terminal idempotency suppresses duplicate network payloads.

Live evidence is recorded on child wf5ro9sa: terminal run 193a0514-0b05-49fa-82ca-83dec652e417 emitted 18 points and flushed successfully; Sentry Trace Metrics queries returned the expected vocabulary and grouping tuple; duplicate run 69c706b4-c123-4c3b-aae7-60172d48808c recorded metricPoints=0 and left Sentry counts unchanged. The DSN is held only in audited Swamp vault factory-observability-sentry and referenced through a vault expression. All requested Deno, pnpm, diff, model, and workflow gates passed. No commit created.

name: Repair SUPERS-25 from Sentry evidence
description:
Sentry SUPERS-25 (issue 7699755376): unhandled promise rejection 'InvalidStateError: Duplicate tool name' on GET / , release gfx@88fe5eb214190a9d604c8db3ad90a7e2303d840e, event 454afdfad0574715b567c0d152422134, 2026-08-29T12:02:05.

WebmcpToolController.#register discards the value document.modelContext.registerTool() returns. In Chrome 152 that is a promise, so a refused registration (duplicate tool name, DOMException code 11) escapes as an unhandled global rejection instead of reaching the caller's catch. The controller also records the tool in #registrations before the browser accepts it, so a refused registration is remembered as owned and never retried.

Fix: make the controller own the registration outcome - await it, drop and abort the bookkeeping entry on refusal, and surface the failure through synchronize() so the layout's existing catch logs it and the next reconcile retries.
result: WebmcpToolController.#register discarded the promise document.modelContext.registerTool() returns, so a refused registration escaped as an unhandled page rejection (InvalidStateError: Duplicate tool name, DOMException code 11) during the layout re-mount teardown race; the refused tool was also recorded as owned and never retried. The controller now awaits the answer, aborts and drops the bookkeeping entry on refusal, and surfaces it through synchronize() where the layout's existing catch logs it and the next reconcile retries. name: Orbit by hand: drag the body to orbit, wheel to dolly, page-grab reframes as today
description: Context: ADR-0060 §4. The only 3D gesture today is grab-the-page reframing of the aim (CanvasEditingOverlay.svelte ~1738-1855, armed at fit zoom on the backdrop element); no wheel handler exists anywhere in src. Work: with the stage on and zoom <= 1, pointerdown on the body candidate (from the canvas-entity leaf) starts an orbit gesture: horizontal drag → yaw, vertical drag → pitch, degrees per pixel scaled by the rendered canvas height (about 90° across the height), clamped to STAGE_CAMERA_POSE_LIMITS, written to the pose the current frame films through (reuse stageCameraPose(): vertical pose under a vertical frame; create a rest pose when none exists, as DepthStageSection's ensurePose does). A wheel event over the canvas at fit zoom with the stage on dollies: distance *= exp(deltaY * k), clamped to minDistance..maxDistance, preventDefault; dragging the page keeps reframing the aim. Each gesture records exactly one compositionEditHistory.recordApplied ('Orbit stage camera' / 'Dolly stage camera') with the before/after pose, bumps measureEpoch so outlines re-project, and invalidates autosave. The math stays in depth-stage-camera.ts (no second camera model); the gesture writes the same fields the StageCameraInspector edits, so the inspector and the export agree. Acceptance: the orbit swings around the aim without moving it; the wheel dollies; limits hold at the extremes; undo restores; the CDP capture of a frame after a gesture matches the inspector's numbers; both orientations.
result: Orbit by hand landed (b3e7965): a drag on the body candidate orbits yaw/pitch (90° per frame height, clamped to STAGE_CAMERA_POSE_LIMITS) and the wheel dollies geometrically, both through stage-camera-editing.ts writers on the frame's pose (vertical-aware, created from rest when absent), each recording one undo entry via the gesture recorder; page-grab reframe unchanged; unit tests for the conversions; verified live: drag changed yaw 14→−10.6 / pitch 4→−8.3 and Cmd+Z restored; wheel dollied 1.9→1.04 and Cmd+Z restored. Note: a whole-document undo drops the selection to the root (existing transaction behaviour).

name: Repair GFX-COMPUTER-2B from Sentry evidence
description:
Sentry GFX-COMPUTER-2B: unhandled 'AbortError: signal is aborted without reason' (event bc93a2fc, 2026-08-31 11:20:17, release gfx@c94ceded9eb38a92599e9327406a3b409e70d8d9 = current main HEAD c94cede). Unhandled promise rejection reported via auto.browser.global_handlers.onunhandledrejection. The DOMException stack points at its construction site: CompositionExportController.cancel -> dispose, reached from Workspace onDestroy while an export was uploading frames (breadcrumbs show PUT /api/export/sessions/vASV-.../frames/3x,4x).

Hypothesis under investigation: html-in-canvas.ts waitForNextPaint creates the 'settled' waiter promise eagerly, then in the rasterization lane returns standardBrowserDomCapture.requestPaint(canvas, signal).then(() => settled). When the abort rejects requestPaint first, the .then callback never runs, so 'settled' — which the abort listener also rejects with signal.reason — is left with no handler and surfaces as an unhandled rejection. Seer's plan (guard cancel(), catch in the upload loop) is advisory and does not match the evidence: abort() cannot throw and the upload rejection is already classified by isCompositionExportCancellation.
result: Fixed. Root cause was NOT in the export controller (Seer's plan was wrong: abort() cannot throw, and the upload rejection is already classified by isCompositionExportCancellation). The orphan was in CanvasPaintGenerationTracker.waitForNextPaint (src/lib/platform/html-in-canvas.ts): in the DOM-rasterization lane it created the 'settled' waiter promise first (required, or a paint landing during the request would be missed), then returned capture.requestPaint(canvas, signal).then(() => settled). One abort rejects both. When the request rejected first, the .then callback never ran, so the waiter's rejection was claimed by nobody and surfaced through the browser's global handler as the unhandled AbortError. Now returns Promise.all([requestPaint, settled]) — both rejections claimed, same contract (the requested pass must complete and its paint record must land). waitForNextPaint gained the lane/scheduler options seam getDomFrameCaptureQueue already exposes, so the cancellation is provable without a DOM. Added a pinning test in html-in-canvas.test.ts that listens for process unhandledRejection; verified red against the old .then form (recorded the AbortError) and green after. pnpm check clean; pnpm test 1792 passed in the worktree and 1793 on integrated main. verify-presets not run: no preset, pack, or pipeline file changed.

name: Serve raw markdown for every docs page
description:
## Context
The site only serves rendered HTML. AI agents consuming GFX docs should fetch markdown, not scrape HTML. All content is in `docs/` markdown at build time; `docs-site/src/lib/server/docs.ts` already enumerates pages (`getAllHrefs`, `buildNav`) and reads sources.

Deliberately absent: **no `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` manifest** — ruled out by Scott 2026-08-31. The convention has no proven consumer uptake, and a navigable site with per-page markdown makes it redundant. Do not add one.

## Work
For every page href, serve a raw-markdown sibling generated at build time: `<href>.md` (e.g. `/preset-format.md`, `/overview.md`) — a prerendered `+server.ts` endpoint returning the page's source markdown with relative links rewritten to site-absolute URLs (reuse/extract the resolution logic from `rewriteHref` — do not duplicate it). Serve as `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`.

## Constraints
- One source of enumeration: derive from the same nav/file listing the HTML pages use, so a new doc automatically gets its `.md` endpoint.
- No runtime filesystem reads on the deployed worker — everything prerendered.
- Strict TS, explicit return types on exports.

## Verification
- `pnpm build` output contains one `.md` per published page.
- A test (or verifiable script run recorded in the result) asserts a sampled `.md` endpoint matches its source doc and contains no relative links.

name: Annotation marks: directional stroke-draw reveal (not fade-in stamp)
description: Surfaced by the research-paper-attention Critic (2026-06-21) and matches the cinematic-audit 'marks appear and sit' deficit. The highlight mark reveals as a saturate-in-place fade: at the first visible frame the band is already ~full width (left edge pinned, right edge barely advances) — coverage/alpha ramps in place rather than a pen pulling left-to-right across the words. aesthetic.md § Mark layer / Motion Vocabulary wants stroke-draw: 'ink saturates along the stroke path over time, never a faded-in stamp.' Make the mark reveal a directional sweep keyed to reading order (left-to-right for highlight/underline/strike; the circle traces its path). High blast radius — affects every annotation mark across the corpus. Non-gating (A-rules don't yet mandate directional draw) but it's the channel mark vocabulary.
result: DONE + verified. Marks now reveal as a directional stroke-draw (steady left-to-right pen drag) instead of a fade-in stamp. Root cause: the mark tween used the preset's named enter ease (smooth=power3.out) which front-loads progress -> the stroke (highlight width / underline+strike length / circle arc, all driven by markProgress) snapped to ~96% in the first few frames then only filled density (the audit's 'marks appear and sit'). Fix: drive the mark draw on a steady power1.inOut (intrinsic to the stroke-draw motion-form, independent of preset ease) in Workspace mark tween. Verified via montage: research-paper-attention highlight sweeps word-by-word p0.17->p0.22 (was full-width by first frame); research-paper-critique renders highlight+underline+circle with no regression. General to all marks in all presets (research-paper-*, quote-*, text-anim-showcase-*). Note: underline/strike (drawMarkerLine) and circle (drawMarkerEllipse) already drew progressively; this makes the pacing steady too. svelte-check clean.

name: Canvas-inspired optical and deformation capability arc
description:
## Goal
Build a clean-room Supers-native family of optical, reveal, deformation, and simulation capabilities inspired by observed CanvasUI behaviors, without importing or porting CanvasUI source, shaders, defaults, assets, or components.

## Why
The current magnify Annotation is visually weak, and the current glass vocabulary is limited to fluted architectural glass. Supers should add physically legible lens/frost/refraction treatments plus deterministic particle, peel, shatter, cloth, fluid, and tiled-deformation motion that works as authored video output rather than interactive website effects.

## Product constraints
- One Preset must render under every Pack and both native orientations.
- Every animation derives from explicit timestamp/frame/progress; no wall-clock or runtime randomness.
- Transparent compositions preserve premultiplied alpha and never paint undeclared backgrounds.
- Final output remains native 3840x2160 or 2160x3840; lower resolutions are allowed only for selected simulation/intermediate fields.
- CanvasUI is behavioral inspiration only. Implement from graphics fundamentals and WICG/WebGPU APIs with independent naming, parameters, shader code, and defaults.
- New Pipelines/domains require a verification Preset and Critic ACCEPT.

## Capability set
- Rebuild focal magnification as a credible optical lens with distortion, edge refraction, controlled chromatic dispersion, haze/frost, and optional Pack-resolved instrument chrome.
- Add non-fluted glass/frost vocabulary: smooth lens glass, frosted/transmission blur, droplets/bubble-style local refraction where compositionally justified.
- Add deterministic particle reveal/dissolve, 3D peel transition, seeded shatter transition, cloth/bend surface deformation, authored fluid/ripple simulation, 2D/3D asset-to-geometry exploration, and tiled deformation.
- Add shared engine seams for dirty DOM generations, pass-local bounds/quality, resource readiness, and seekable stateful GPU simulation where required.

## Done when
Every child epic/task is completed with tests, native horizontal+vertical proving renders, transparent-alpha verification where applicable, GUI schema/editor parity, updated current-truth docs/ADR, and Critic ACCEPT for each new Pipeline family verification Preset.
result: Completed the clean-room optical and deformation capability arc. Shipped rebuilt Magnify plus refractive-lens/frosted-glass optics; render-efficiency and readiness seams; typed particle-dissolve, sheet-peel, and seeded-shatter transitions; a deterministic fixed-step seek/reset/replay runtime; fluid-ripple, cloth-bend, and tiled-deformation Effects; GUI editors, schemas, fixtures, tests, and current-truth ADR/docs. ADR-0047 rejects broad asset-to-geometry import until a bounded Pipeline needs it. Independent Critics ACCEPTed the optical showcase and all six new transition/material/deformation fixtures at native horizontal and vertical. Final verification passed: git diff --check, npm run check, verify-presets, test:structural, build, test:browser, and npm test (75 files, 342 tests). No commit was created because none was requested.

Then sized the pointer to the frame (was fixed 32px = 0.8% of 4K, unreadable -> frame.width*0.024 ≈92px) + trail width/length + drop-shadow. name: User-defined Packs — data-authored packs behind a UserPackStore
description:
## Goal
Ship [ADR-0055](docs/adr/0055-user-defined-packs.md): a User Pack is a validated JSON pack document living in the user's files — authored, edited, and selected like a User composition — renderable in the engine but never part of the creator catalog. The surface is the drafting lane for the concierge pack pipeline: iterate a look live with no repo commit per tweak; promotion to catalog stays the authoring playbook + Calibration Trio.

## Boundaries that bind every task
- PackManifest stays the document shape (src/lib/platform/packs/types.ts) — roles as data, fonts as declarations. Save-time validation reuses src/lib/platform/packs/validation.ts and fails closed.
- User pack slugs never shadow PACK_REGISTRY slugs; resolution is built-ins first, user store second; a missing user pack fails with an actionable error, never a silent substitute.
- Fonts: Google Fonts only, validated against a vendored catalog manifest (never synthesize cuts), materialized into a hash-pinned same-origin cache at save time. Render time never touches a third party.
- User packs never enter PACK_CATALOG_REGISTRY, never produce verification evidence; verify-presets / probe-pack-diff / calibration bundles / layout-contract matrix stay scoped to PACK_REGISTRY. ADR-0039 neutrality is judged against catalog packs only.
- Disk-backed store + font cache are development-profile only (ADR-0053); the public profile's routes refuse.
- Every authoring capability is an appearance-family row in the WebMCP operation inventory (ADR-0054). No new family, no new transport.

## Done when
A user forks a built-in pack into their store from the GUI, edits its roles and fonts, sees compositions render under it (preview == export), an agent does the same through WebMCP tools, and pnpm check / test / verify-presets stay green with user packs invisible to all deliverable gates.
result: User-defined Packs shipped 2026-09-01 in seven leaves: Google Fonts catalog + font-claim validation; same-origin hash-pinned font cache; UserPackStore + /api/user-packs; source-aware resolution (builtins first, user store second, fail closed); Pack control fork/edit/select/delete (approved by Scott on gfx-review with the Sentry pack); WebMCP appearance rows + evals; docs closure with ADR-0055 Canon.

name: Make Factory observability automatic and lifecycle-wide
description:
## Goal
Make Sentry observability an automatic, non-gating part of every Supers Planning and Delivery Factory lifecycle so we can measure effectiveness, profile stage performance, and diagnose Factory failures.

name: Gate rendering on the canvas flag; one combined-flag browser; mothball the fallback lane
description:
## Decision (Scott, 2026-08-31 — post-descope reconciliation)
The DOM-rasterization fallback existed solely for the descoped public demo. Locally it silently serves degraded renders and made the same URL look different across browsers. Kill that behavior:

1. Hard capability gate: if CanvasDrawElement is absent, the app renders NOTHING approximate — it shows a plain full-screen notice naming the required flag with the exact copyable launch command. No degraded lane reachable from the app, ever.
2. Combined-flag browser: launch-cdp-chrome.sh gains a mode with --enable-blink-features=CanvasDrawElement,WebMCP (flags are comma-separable) so agents drive WebMCP against the REAL renderer; make it the default for local agent use; document in AGENTS.md.
3. Mothball dom-rasterization: unreachable from app code paths (kept in-tree for a possible future public demo); rescope the authoring scenario + agent evals + browser-render matrix to the combined-flag mode; remove/repoint standard-lane assertions so suites stay green and meaningful.
4. window.__gfxDomFrameCaptureMode reporting stays truthful (canvas-draw-element or absent+gated).

## Done when
An unflagged browser shows the notice (no canvas, no approximation); a combined-flag browser renders canonically with all WebMCP tools registered; suites green; AGENTS.md documents the single-browser story.
result: Rendering hard-gates on CanvasDrawElement: unflagged browsers get only the full-screen notice (WICG html-in-canvas link + chrome://flags/#canvas-draw-element + copyable launch command), no degraded lane reachable. launch-cdp-chrome.sh gained the combined agent mode (CanvasDrawElement+WebMCP, port 9229), documented as the default local agent browser. dom-rasterization mothballed (@deprecated, unreachable from app). GET /api/user-compositions/<slug> answered 500 'Corrupt preset data' when a stored composition read fine and parsed but failed a rule tightened after it was saved; hooks.server.ts promotes every 5xx, so each open of the author's own composition filed a Sentry issue. name: Make Sentry reproduction and coding autonomous
description:
## Goal
Turn the Sentry loop into outcome-producing automation: recent unresolved issues must queue deterministic reproduction on HEAD, confirmed failures must create or attach one Dex repair task, and Delivery must code the fix automatically.

## Required behavior
- Exact HEAD release attribution identifies evidence; absence is never treated as proof of a fix.
- Recent unresolved issues enter a bounded WIP-one reproduction queue even when another Dex task is active; existing work delays execution but does not discard intents.
- Reproduction runs the affected local flow against HEAD and records positive failure or bounded no-reproduction evidence.
- Confirmed failures create or attach exactly one Dex task, start Planning/Delivery automatically, dispatch Pi coding through the existing trusted Factory boundary, and retain replay-safe identities.
- Ambiguous duplicates, destructive/high-risk repairs, incomplete evidence, and repeated failed reproduction remain quarantined.
- Successful integrated fixes replay the reproduction flow and resolve Sentry only from exact post-fix evidence.

## Done when
A scheduled Swamp workflow takes a recent non-HEAD Sentry issue through queued reproduction, deduplicated Dex creation, automatic code Delivery, post-fix verification, and idempotent Sentry resolution without a manual bridge command; tests cover retries, WIP queueing, release silence, duplicates, and failure quarantine; live canary evidence proves one full path.
result: Scheduled six-hour Swamp self-healing now reproduces code-owned local failures on exact HEAD, immediately admits independent repairs without a capacity gate, dispatches Pi in isolated worktrees, serializes verified integration, scopes verification to the exact receipt, preserves human gates for visual work, completes non-visual machine repairs through terminal Factory evidence, checks fresh no-recurrence, and resolves Sentry in the exact integrated release. Live canary SUPERS-20 resolved in supers@698efe055b3c03ebdcb35cd9b59088aee8c163c5 with terminal Dex task xx72rz60 and resolution receipt d51b810ddd77088a9b710b88e5ca1b28ca753ad4e679cd2fc9065b0cf65c838e. Verification: 262 Factory tests, 16 handoff tests, pnpm check, and 873 Vitest tests passed.

name: Audit published docs pages for accuracy against current state
description:
## Context
The site publishes `docs/` as-is, and several published pages predate recent reality: the 2026-08-31 public-deployment descope (local-first, gfx.computer = docs only), the client-side rendering change (commit 8c57560), and the current pipeline/pack registries. The north star is *accurate* documentation for AI — a stale page is worse than a missing one.

## Work
Sweep every page the site publishes in nav sections Start, Engine, Authoring, Quality, and Packs (skip Decisions/ADRs and Ideas — ADRs are historical records and are never rewritten) and fix statements that are false today. Priority checks:
- `docs/README.md`, `docs/engine-architecture.md`, `docs/html-in-canvas-typegpu.md`: rendering path claims vs the client-side rendering change; deployment/hosting claims vs the descope (ADR-0052/0053).
- `docs/preset-format.md`: variant lists vs the live pipeline registries (`src/lib/pipelines/*`, `src/lib/platform/pipelines/definition-registry.ts`).
- Pack aesthetic docs vs the shipped packs.
Fix in the `docs/` sources; where a doc names counts, flags, ports, or commands, verify each against the code before keeping it.

## Constraints
- Never rewrite ADRs, `docs/history/`, or `.dex/` content (ADR-0053).
- Fix accuracy, not voice — no wholesale rewrites; smallest edit that makes the statement true.
- Legacy `supers` spellings follow ADR-0053 dispositions — run `pnpm check:names` after edits.

## Verification
- Result lists every page audited and every edit made (or "accurate as-is").
- `pnpm check:names` and `pnpm audit:planning` pass; docs-site `pnpm build` passes.
result: Audited all 14 published docs pages (Start/Engine/Authoring/Quality/Packs) against current code; fixed six false statements: removed the claimed public gfx.computer demo (post-descope), corrected the crt-terminal chrome attribution (crt-tube at curvature 0, not crt-screen), added missing brand-mark Surface + lower-third standard/cinematic variants to preset-format, corrected stale browser guidance, plus README/roadmap staleness. name: Effect keyframe rows in the inspector and an effect row on the timeline
description:
## Scope
Context: ADR-0063 §9 (`docs/adr/0063-keyframed-effect-parameters.md`). `src/lib/platform/KeyframesSection.svelte` holds the DaVinci-style row for surface, overlay, and block owners: value at the playhead, ◀ ◆ ▶, ease-into while parked on a keyframe, with `upsertKeyframe`, `toggleKeyframe`, `jump`, `setValue`, `setEase`, and `normalizeEases` in its script. Effect Editors under `src/lib/pipelines/effects/*/Editor.svelte` are hand-written `<label class="row">` inputs bound to `effect.params`; `src/lib/platform/EffectChainRow.svelte` mounts one Editor per authored effect. `src/lib/platform/composition-timeline-tracks.ts` builds rows (`clipKeyframes`, `makeKeyframeRetimer`, `makeKeyframeDeleter`, `cascadeLinkFor`, `writeCascadeStart`); `src/lib/platform/timeline-entity-identity.ts` defines track identities and keyframe selection ids. Live channel values sit in `animState.effectChannels` (runtime leaf).

Build:
- Extract the per-channel row into `src/lib/platform/KeyframeChannelRow.svelte` (label, bounds and integer flag, the owner's `animation` block, clip start in ms, the live value, and a static read/write pair used when the row has no track). Move the pure logic (keyframe index at the playhead, upsert with ease normalization, jump candidates, clamping) into a colocated `.ts` module so `KeyframesSection` and the effect rows share one implementation. `KeyframesSection` composes the row with no change in behavior or look.
- `src/lib/platform/EffectParamRow.svelte`: one numeric param of an effect rendered through `KeyframeChannelRow`, with bounds and integer flag from `listEffectKeyframeChannels`. Without a track it edits `effect.params` at the dotted path; ◆ starts a track at the playhead from the current value; with a track it edits the keyframe at the playhead and reads its live value from `animState.effectChannels`. Convert every effect Editor's numeric rows to it and keep selects, colors, and checkboxes as they are; frozen params render as plain rows without ◆.
- Timeline: `TimelineTrackIdentity` gains `{ kind: 'effect'; effectId }` (`effect:<id>`, parse round-trip, keyframe selection ids through it). Build a row per authored effect that has a channel or a cascade, labelled with the Effect label, with diamonds from `clipKeyframes`, retime and delete handlers, and the cascade tether from `cascadeLinkFor`. An unwelded bar has no `onUpdate` and is not draggable; a welded bar drags its offset through `writeCascadeStart`. Selecting a diamond focuses the effect (`CompositionWorkspaceFocus` already has `{ target: 'effect' }`).
- Undo: every row edit and timeline drag records one edit-history entry the way the overlay rows do.

Constraints: no `$effect` unless unavoidable; no rename-only `$derived`; Graffiti tokens and the existing `.kf-row` styling, no new CSS variants; no new sections, labels, or explanatory text; the effect row must be indistinguishable from an overlay keyframe row.

## Done when
`pnpm check` and `pnpm test` are green. A `*.dom.test.ts` for `KeyframeChannelRow` (add, remove, jump, ease) and for `EffectParamRow` (static edit versus keyframe edit, frozen param without ◆) in the `dom` project. `composition-timeline-tracks.test.ts` covers the effect row, its absence without channels or a weld, and the welded drag. Existing KeyframesSection and overlay tests pass unchanged. After integration Scott can open any Preset on gfx.robo.online, add Pixelation, press ◆ on Pixel size at two playhead positions, and scrub the result.

name: Resolve optical Critic round-two findings
description:
## Goal
Resolve the post-R2 Critic findings preventing optical-lens-showcase ACCEPT.

## Pipeline findings
- Frosted-glass sparse 17-tap transmission produces discrete repeated glyph ghosts instead of continuous rough scattering.
- Magnify hardcodes visible iris entry/exit to 10% of Mark progress, yielding ~66 ms transitions and violating Q15/G6 for legal Mark durations.
- Paper Surface vertical reflow places readable content at x=29 and source label near y=3494, outside title/platform safe areas.

## Preset findings
- Focal frame has four perceptual saturated hue clusters; Q4 allows at most three.
- Frost growth spans 720 ms; G6 entry window is 250-400 ms.
- Surface exit is 33.3% shorter than entry; G6 requires 20-30%.

## Requirements
Fix defects in owning Pipeline/default code, not by hiding them in the Preset. Tune only findings classified preset-choice. Preserve deterministic native horizontal/vertical rendering, alpha-safe compositing, and Pack neutrality.

## Done when
Focused tests, npm run check, npm run verify-presets, npm run build, native captures/probes, and a fresh isolated Critic all pass with zero pipeline-bug/default-too-permissive findings.
result: Resolved round-two frost ghosting, Magnify timing, vertical safe-area reflow, hue count, frost growth, and Surface exit findings. Frost now uses a 169-tap isotropic gaussian kernel and all timing/safety gates pass.

## Scope
- Separate universal lifecycle-integrity checks from domain verification.
- Remove unconditional all-Preset corpus verification from policy-sweep.
- Add typed pre-implementation work-domain routing that selects skills/constraints but can only add, never suppress, trusted path-derived obligations.
- Refine trusted post-integration change-impact classification and fanout into smallest-complete lanes, including affected Preset verification, app browser checks, render/Pack matrices, export decode, performance evidence, Swamp model/workflow validation, and planning/docs checks.
- Mixed changes take the exact union. Unknown classifications pause as unavailable instead of guessing or running unrelated suites.
- Preserve exact work-item, integration-receipt, revision, changed-path, tree-fingerprint, workflow-run, and evidence correlation.
- Compile/materialize the Supers Delivery profile only after contracts and fixtures pass.

## Acceptance matrix
- Swamp-only change: no Preset, browser, or render checks.
- App-only change: no corpus or render matrix.
- Direct Preset change: affected Preset scope, not automatically all Presets.
- Broad render change: full required render scope and aesthetic gate.
- Performance change: declared benchmark evidence plus touched-subsystem checks.
- Export change: export/decode checks.
- Documentation/planning change: discoverability/planning checks only.
- Mixed change: exact union of applicable lanes.
- Unknown change: evidence-unavailable pause.

## Verification
Fixture-test every route and exclusion, validate affected selectors, validate all changed Swamp models/workflows, run relevant Factory/control-plane suites, materialize safely, and record live no-op route proofs.
result: Supers Delivery now routes implementation guidance and deterministic verification by typed task intent plus trusted integrated paths, with unrelated Preset/browser/render lanes excluded.

name: Repair GFX-COMPUTER-2C from Sentry evidence
description:
Sentry GFX-COMPUTER-2C: '503 GET /api/health', 2 events 2026-08-31T22:32:12-13, release gfx@6143cc6, environment development, host dev-gfx.robo.online via curl.

Body: {"status":"unavailable","release":"gfx@6143cc6...","checks":{"ffmpeg":"ok","temporaryDisk":"unavailable"}}

The 503 itself is CORRECT. Measured on the host: statfs(tmpdir()) reports bavail*bsize = 4469063680 (4.2 GiB) against PUBLIC_EXPORT_RUNTIME_LIMITS.requiredTemporaryDiskBytes = 8 GiB. inspectTemporaryDisk mkdtemp'd and wrote its probe successfully, so the directory exists and is writable — Seer's plan (mkdir the temp dir at startup) is wrong and fixes nothing.

The defect is observability, not readiness: logErrorResponses in src/hooks.server.ts promotes EVERY resolved 5xx via Sentry.captureMessage, and /api/health's 503 is the readiness contract's designed 'not ready' answer (ADR-0052; the route doc says '200 once the host can serve both export lanes, 503 while it cannot'). A container healthcheck polling an unready host files one High-priority Sentry error per poll, drowning real errors.

Fix: classify a designed status response in src/lib/platform/public-error-observability.ts (the module that already owns the promote/redact policy and is deliberately Node-free) so /api/health's 503 logs but does not promote.
result: Fixed. The 503 was correct — the host had 4.2 GiB free temp disk against the 8 GiB PUBLIC_EXPORT_RUNTIME_LIMITS.requiredTemporaryDiskBytes reserves, and inspectTemporaryDisk's mkdtemp + probe write both succeeded, so the directory was present and writable (Seer's mkdir-at-startup plan would have fixed nothing). The defect was in observability: logErrorResponses promoted every resolved 5xx, and /api/health's 503 is the ADR-0052 readiness contract's designed 'not ready' answer that the container healthcheck polls on a loop — one High-priority Sentry error per poll on an unready host. Added isDesignedResponseStatus + DESIGNED_RESPONSE_STATUSES_BY_PATHNAME to src/lib/platform/public-error-observability.ts (the module that already owns the promote/redact policy and stays Node-free so hook and tests read one rule); describeErrorResponse now returns diagnostic: null for a designed status, so the readiness 503 still logs with its body but is never promoted. A genuine 500 from the same route still promotes. Corrected the now-stale 'promote every resolved 5xx' comment in src/hooks.server.ts. Two tests added in public-error-observability.test.ts pinning the exact Sentry observation; verified both fail with the classifier neutralized. pnpm check green (0 errors, lint/discoverability/names/spawn-hygiene pass) and pnpm test green (188 files, 1841 tests). No preset/pack/pipeline files touched, so verify-presets did not apply.

name: Repair SUPERS-28 from Sentry evidence
description:
SUPERS-28 AbortError: Export session cancelled. (issue 7701267455), first/last seen 2026-08-30 14:24:28, release supers@840151e (ancestor of main), mechanism auto.function.sveltekit.handle_error, transaction POST /api/export/sessions/[sessionId]/complete, file app:///export-session.server.ts fn #dispose.

Root cause (confirmed by reading main): ExportSessionStore.#dispose (src/lib/platform/export-session.server.ts:1070) aborts session.abortController with a raw DOMException AbortError. Any concurrent uploadAudio/uploadFrame/complete awaiting that signal rejects with that raw DOMException. Both route handlers (complete/+server.ts:18, frames/[frame]/+server.ts:25) map only ExportSessionError and rethrow everything else, so SvelteKit turns an expected cancellation into a 500 and reports it to Sentry.

Same cluster, same traces: SUPERS-29 (500 POST complete, trace da1c5c83) and SUPERS-27 Error: aborted / SUPERS-26 + SUPERS-2A (500 PUT frames/1, traces 482949ad + 9bbc4164) - a client disconnect aborts request.signal and escapes by the identical path.

Fix direction: classify an abort inside the store and surface it as a typed ExportSessionError with a defined status, so a cancelled session or a departed client is a client outcome rather than a server fault.
result: Fixed: a cancelled or client-abandoned export now answers 410 instead of escaping the route as an unhandled 500. Added classifyExportSessionFailure in src/lib/platform/export-session.server.ts, called in the catch of uploadAudio/uploadFrame/complete BEFORE #dispose (disposal aborts the session controller, so classifying after would relabel every deliberate refusal a cancellation). ExportSessionError passes through unchanged; a genuine fault still escapes raw as a 500; only a real abort becomes 410. Tests: the existing request-abort test now pins the 410 instead of the raw escape, a new test covers the SUPERS-28 concurrent-cancel-during-frame-upload path, and the crashed-encoder test asserts it is NOT relabelled 410. Both new assertions verified to fail with the classifier disabled. Also added the two files to the existing frozen SUPERS-<n> declared surface in scripts/check-legacy-name-dispositions.mjs (ADR-0053 already scopes 'every issue ever cited by short id'). pnpm check green; pnpm test 1787/1787 across 182 files green. Note: pnpm test:structural fails on scripts/test-workspace-render-seam.ts ('the shared frame seam must own the only live DOM upload operation', 2 !== 1) - reproduced identically on clean main, touches only composition-frame-renderer.ts which this change never modified, so it is pre-existing and unrelated. Same root cause also covers SUPERS-27/26/29/2A, left unresolved for a separate run.

name: Rubric: G5 avg-ink phase tolerance for material-texture chromes
description: From the title-sequence-drop-crt Critic (ACCEPT 2026-07-10) + show-open rounds 4-5: under a deterministic material chrome (mask lattice + beam raster + shimmer), small-caps avg-ink oscillates a few percent with texture phase — the drop piece's kicker measures mean 4.53 across the hold but 4.43-4.46 on 2 of 7 frames with every lever at documented max. name: Source-aware pack resolution: builtins first, user store second, fail closed
description:
## Context
ADR-0055: `getPack` (`src/lib/platform/packs/registry.ts`) is a static builtin lookup today. Compositions must resolve packs through a two-source chain — `PACK_REGISTRY` first, then the user store — while every deliverable verification gate stays scoped to builtins only, and a composition naming an absent user pack fails with an actionable error, never a silent substitute.

## Work
1. Source-aware resolution where compositions resolve their pack: `composition-frame-renderer.ts`, appearance var resolution, and the export path all accept a user-store-resolved `PackManifest`. Boot-time builtin validation is unchanged; user manifests were validated at save and revalidate cheaply on load.
2. Missing-user-pack failure surfaced in the GUI and in operation receipts with the pack slug and the recovery action.
3. `appearance.set-pack` (`src/lib/platform/webmcp-operation-inventory.ts`) accepts user pack slugs — extend the live-registry enum derivation to include user store slugs per ADR-0054 (never register a tool that cannot succeed in the current state).
4. `fontsReady` active-pack gating (prior task) proven on preview AND export for a user-pack-bound composition.
5. Guard test asserting `verify-presets`, `probe-pack-diff`, calibration bundle inputs, and the layout-contract matrix enumerate `PACK_REGISTRY` only — user packs are invisible to all deliverable evidence.

## Verification
Unit tests for the resolution chain + fail-closed error; one deterministic scripted CDP pass (the `scripts/cdp-*.mjs` harness per the canvas-verification rule — never the MCP browser) rendering a fixture composition bound to a seeded user pack; `pnpm verify-presets` green and unchanged in scope; `pnpm check` + `pnpm test` green.
result: Source-aware resolution: getPack consults a runtime User Pack source; ensurePackLoaded loads store packs before every path that names a pack; UnknownPackError fails closed; packScope registry/runtime/stored on preset semantic validation; fontsReady sweeps loaded user packs; deliverable gates guarded registry-only; pnpm probe:user-pack-render CDP pass green.

name: Design the lifecycle observability contract
description: Define automatic terminal routing, outcome mapping, profiling signals, receipt coverage, and non-gating failure semantics for Planning and Delivery.
result:
Defined the lifecycle observability contract:
- Observability is a required lifecycle stage before every terminal state, not a manual post-run command.
- Each outcome-specific observability stage runs one factory-specific workflow that first advances to the real terminal state, then invokes summary and the Sentry emitter as allowFailure steps. Sentry availability cannot alter the terminal outcome.
- Delivery covers done and aborted. Planning covers done, rejected, parked, failed-apply, failed-audit, and aborted; custom failure terminals retain their exact failedStage while the canonical broad outcome remains parked.
- The emitter remains the single network boundary and expands bounded metrics for stage visits/dispatches/time-to-gate, human touches, and failed terminal stage so Sentry supports profiling and diagnosis as well as completion counts.
- Both reusable profile compilers gain optional terminal-observer workflow configuration so materialization cannot erase the wiring and consumers without an observer remain backward compatible.
- A Swamp-native coverage method will compare every terminal state/journal key against emitter receipts. Missing coverage is explicit local data and a failing audit gate, not silent dashboard absence.
- Normal lifecycle verification must prove automatic receipt creation; direct invocation of the telemetry workflow is not acceptable evidence.
Architecture basis: Swamp workflows orchestrate multiple model methods; the emitter model owns the external Sentry action; reports remain deterministic analysis only, consistent with the Swamp architecture guide and docs/project-control-plane.md.
